text:
Run Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow
Run Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow
The purpose of the run stage in the VSO.ai workflow is to run the VSO.ai selected tests
and record the results. The run stage comprises the following three steps:
• Ask Step
• Execute Step
• Tell Step
Ask Step
VSO.ai intelligently selects a set of tests by using the ask command in the Run stage of
the VSO.ai workflow. Each selected test run is associated with a unique run_id and some
additional run arguments that VSO.ai returns. The command is as follows:
--ask [{N, all, runs:N, runs:all, cpu[:C[X]]}] \
[--out <filename>] \
[--fmt {csv, json, shell}] \
[--simstats]
• If –-ask N or –-ask runs:N is specified, VSO.ai returns a list of the next N tests that
should be run, with each entry having all the earlier fields.
• If –-ask all or –-ask runs:all is specified, VSO.ai returns a list of all the tests that
should be run to meet the target criteria with each entry having all the earlier fields
from. Note that this is an estimated list and the final coverage might not actually meet
the targeted goal because of constrained random tests and changes to the RTL and
testbench.
Additionally, unless a --exit cpu[:C[X]] or –-exit runs:R option is specified
during the init step. The -–exit fails:F option is ignored with --ask all .
If cpu[:C[X]] is specified, VSO.ai returns a list of tests where the projected run times
of this list of tests is closest to the total time taken by the default regression.
◦ If C is used, VSO.ai returns a list of tests where the projected run times of this list of
tests is closest to C hours.
◦ If CX is used, VSO.ai returns a list of tests where the projected run times of this list
of tests is closest to C times the total time takes by the default regression run.
• --workdir <workdir> specifies the working directory.

Run Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow
• --out FILENAME , if specified, the output is written to FILENAME. If not, the output is
written to the standard out.
• --fmt, if specified, the output format matches the requested format. .csv is the default
format.
The following is the output from the ask step in the CSV format (single line):
CSO_RESULT:TEST=<TEST_NAME> BUILD=<BUILD_NAME> RUN_ID=<RUN_ID>
SEED=<SEED_VALUE> SEED_TYPE=<SEED_TYPE> PHASE=<PHASE_NAME>
PEAK_MEMORY=<PEAK_MEMORY>
◦ TEST_NAME is the name of the test template selected to run, such as testname.
◦ BUILD_NAME is the name of the build selected to run, such as buildname.
◦ RUN_ID is the VSO.ai-specific run_id for this ask to be passed to the simulation job.
◦ SEED_TYPE is a type of the seed value, for example, “failure” or “golden”.
◦ SEED_VALUE is a possible random seed to be used for this test run. If SEED_TYPE is
failure or golden, VSO.ai expects that seed to be used for this run. If it is blank,
you can either use the suggested seed or disregard it and supply your own random
seed.
◦ PHASE_NAME is the name of the VSO.ai phase that this run was selected for, that is
Stress, Acceleration, or Exploration.
◦ PEAK_MEMORY represents the peak projected memory for this test if the –-simstats
option is passed to the ask step.
This is an estimate based on a combination of historical evidence and
accounting for any RTL changes made to the current design. This can be
used to select the appropriate scheduler queue for the job.
• If –-fmt json is specified, the output is a dictionary in the JSON format, with each
tuple from above converted into a key value pair.
If –-fmt shell is specified, the output is of the form <key>=<value> that can be used
in a shell script.
• --simstats, if specified, the output of this step also contains the estimated peak
memory for the test.

Run Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow
VSO.ai relies on the YAML configuration file to determine the constitution of the
default regression run. If the configuration file is not specified during the current
init step, it relies on the last version that was seen and saved in the dbdir.
VSO.ai uses historical data to determine the average run time for each of the
tests. The actual run times for the tests in the current regression run can vary
depending on multiple factors such as code changes, random seed, machine
configuration and load.
Execute Step
In the execute step of the Run stage in the VSO.ai workflow, the user is responsible for
running the simulation job corresponding to the VSO.ai selected build/test by passing it the
VSO.ai suggested parameters. The command is as follows:
<simv> \
-vso_opts workdir=<workdir> \
-vso_opts run_id=<RUN_ID> \
+ntb_random_seed=<SEED_VALUE> \
<other simv options>
• other simv options specifies the simv options required to turn on the code and
functional coverage dumping for Day0 or Relearn runs.
If the returned SEED_TYPE is not failure or golden and you want to discard the VSO.ai
returned SEED_VALUE, the following option can be used to generate a different random
seed for this run instead of the +ntb_random_seed option:
+ntb_random_seed_automatic
Tell Step
When the simulation run has completed, VSO.ai needs to know the result of the simulation
to determine the current state of failures and coverage for the regression run. By default,
VSO.ai includes the coverage from a failing test in its targeting and reporting. If this is not
required, the –-ignore_failed option can be used during the init step. The result of
the simulation run is given to VSO.ai in the Tell step of the Run stage using the following
--tell <RUN_ID> \
[--failed [signature]]

Finalization Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow

• --failed is specified if the test run failed.
• signature is a comma-separated list of signatures the test failed with. The signature
can be any user-defined string and is used by VSO.ai to target all unique failure
signatures during the Stress phase in the subsequent regression runs. It also notifies
VSO.ai that a particular failure signature has been covered in the current regression
run so that it can focus its effort on other failure signatures.

VSO.ai that a particular failure signature has been covered in the current regression

VSO.ai uses an approximate proxy for coverage. Additionally, VSO.ai reports a
coverage percentage based on the total number of covered bins from the last
regression run that was merged in dbdir. Therefore, the coverage percentages
reported by VSO.ai in the tell output may not match the actual URG coverage
score.
Finalization Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow
The purpose of the finalization stage in the VSO.ai workflow is to notify VSO.ai that the
regression is complete. VSO.ai then proceeds to generate the results of the regression run
and create the learning from this regression run so that it could be merged into the central
dbdir.
The VSO.ai report uses an approximate proxy for coverage. Therefore, the
coverage percentages reported by VSO.ai are not exactly the same as what
URG reports. You should always use URG even for a VSO.ai regression to
determine the exact coverage score.
The Finalization stage comprises the following steps:
• Finalize Step
• Report Step
• Merge Step
Finalize Step
The finalize step of the Finalization stage in the VSO.ai workflow uses the following
command to notify VSO.ai that the regression run has completed:
--finalize \

Finalization Stage in the VSO.ai Workflow
--workdir <workdir>
The finalize step aggregates all the warnings and error messages from each of the log
files into a single file. And any log files (except from the main online.log and tell.log
files) that do not have any errors or warnings are deleted.
The –-analytics option to get an updated status of the regression.
Report Step
The report step in the Finalization stage of the VSO.ai workflow is optional. By default,
the finalize step automatically generates a report for the regression run. Reports can,
however, be used to generate an intermediate report while the regression run is still
ongoing. This can be done by using the following command:
--report \
[--reportdir REPORTDIR]
The report is available in the workdir/report directory by default, unless --reportdir
is used. When --reportdir is specified, the report is available in REPORTDIR. The
generated report is currently a statically generated HTML page that can be opened in a
browser. To view this report, run the following command:
firefox <vso_workdir>/report/index.html
This is scheduled to change in the next release to be a server hosted report.
Merge Step
VSO.ai uses transfer learning to retain the information about the covered coverage targets
and failures to merge them in the next run. Transfer learning is the ability to capture the
knowledge from the previous regressions to enhance results in the future runs.
If a regression run is successful and has meaningful data, it is recommended that the
merge step should be invoked in the Finalization stage of the workflow so that VSO.ai can
leverage the learning from the current regression runs in future regression runs. This is
done by invoking the following command:
--merge \
--dbdir <dbdir > \
[--out <outdir>]

Simplified Use Model of VSO.ai
This step merges the learnings of this regression run from the workdir into the dbdir if
the --out option is not specified.
Figure 3 Merge Step
This figure is a pictorial representation of the different steps.
Configure, Compile and Init are part of the Initialization stage.
Ask, Execute and Tell are part of the Run stage.
And Finalize and Merge are part of the Finalize stage. Ask, Execute, and Tell are in a
loop depending on the number of Ask steps invoked.
dbdir is the reference VSO.ai model directory where the learning across regression runs
is stored. workdir specifies the directory to use for this regression run and is accessed by
every step in the flow, both for reading and writing.
Simplified Use Model of VSO.ai
The VSO.ai Ask-Tell interface has multiple benefits:
• Tell gives VSO.ai an accurate picture of the current state of regression, which VSO.ai
uses to update its ML model online. It allows VSO.ai to leverage reinforcement
learning. VSO.ai can dynamically adapt its test recommendations to achieve the
remaining goals based on what is achieved thus far in a regression.

text:
Simplified Use Model of VSO.ai
However, it is possible to trade-off QoR for ease of use to make it easy to deploy VSO.ai in
the regression environment. VSO.ai supports a three-step flow that involves the following
steps:
1. Configure VSO.ai and compile each build by using the following VCS compile
$VCS_HOME/bin/vcs \
-vso_opts buildname=<buildname> \
[other VCS options]
2. Get a test list of all tests to be run and run each of the suggested tests. This is done by
chaining the init and ask steps using the following command:
--init \
--ask all \
--pre_init “<pre_init_script script_options>” \
--regr_config <config_file> \
--target_metric <metric_list> \
[VSO grid options] \
[other VSO init options] \
[other VSO ask options]
Run all the predicted simulation jobs, passing all the relevant options as described in
the execute step:
<simv> \
-vso_opts workdir=<workdir> \
-vso_opts run_id=<RUN_ID> \
+ntb_random_seed=<SEED_VALUE> \
<other simv options>
3. Finalize the result after the regression has completed. This is done by chaining the
finalize and merge steps and providing the failures in bulk by using the following
--finalize \
--merge \
[--update_fails <csv file> ]
--update_fails records all the failures in the <csv file> in bulk.

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
Wrapper Interface in VSO.ai
Refer to Recording Failures for more information.
Wrapper Interface in VSO.ai
In the Run Stage, the three steps in the workflow, that is, ask, execute, and tell through
the Ask-Tell interface provide maximum flexibility and controllability. However, it does
require additional efforts to integrate with the existing regression environments. VSO.ai
provides a Wrapper Use Model to simplify the integration of VSO.ai for simple regression
environments. In this case, VSO.ai performs all the steps of the regression, including the
execute phase where it launches the simulation jobs on the grid. The Wrapper Use Model
has limitations as VSO.ai is the one initiating the simulation. For example, it is possible
that a configuration or test chosen by VSO.ai requires prerequisites to be established
before running. Therefore, it is primarily recommended for proof-of-concept trials. The
advantage is its ease of integration with the existing regression scripts.
Using the Wrapper Use Model requires the test execution options to be added to the
VSO.ai configuration file using the arguments keyword. For a single build, if the execution
options for all tests of the single build are the same, the execution command line can be
specified as an argument to --online. The arguments line in the configuration file is not
required. In this case, the --online option should be the last option passed to the driver
command since VSO.ai considers all options after --online to be the simv execution
command.
config_name: ubus

text:
- name: cfg1
simv_location: "/path/to/cfg1/simv"
comp_vdb_path: "/path/to/cfg1/compile vdb"

- name: cfg2
simv_location: "/path/to/cfg2/simv"
comp_vdb_path: "/path/to/cfg2/compile vdb"

- name: test_r8_w8_r4_w4
build: cfg1
count: 100
arguments: -vso cso -lca -vso_opts testname=test_r8_w8_r4_w4 -cm_name
test_r8_w8_r4_w4_$${EMAN_RANDOM} +UVM_TESTNAME=test_r8_w8_r4_w4
+ntb_random_seed=$${EMAN_RANDOM} ${common_opts}

- name: test_2m_4s
build: cfg2
count: 100
arguments: -vso cso -lca -vso_opts testname=test_2m_4s
-cm_name test_2m_4s _$${EMAN_RANDOM} +UVM_TESTNAME=test_2m_4s
+ntb_random_seed=$${EMAN_RANDOM} ${common_opts}

Wrapper Interface in VSO.ai
For more information on how to create configuration file with the complete
information for the Wrapper interface instead of the Ask-Tell interface, refer to
Appendix D: Configuration File.
The command to enable the Wrapper User Model is as follows:
--regr_config <config_file> \
--target_metric <metric_list> \
[VSO grid options] \
[other VSO options] \
--online <path_to_build_simv> <simv options>

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
Visualization in VSO.ai
The purpose of dashboards in VSO.ai is to visualize, analyze, and track the key metrics
related to software testing and coverage. The Analytics Dashboard provides insights
into coverage metrics, progress tracking, and trend analysis across the three regression
phases of VSO.ai.
Use Model to Access the Analytics Dashboard
After the init step is completed, users can access the analytics dashboard in VSO.ai by
using the following command:
$driver --analytics --workdir <vso workdir> --port <port>
The driver --analytics command starts a server in the specified port (8001 by default)
enabling users to view the analytics dashboard in a web browser such as, Firefox.
The same use model applies to the compare flow as well.
The following sections describe the various regression phases, the available dashboards
in VSO.ai, and the data these dashboards provide across the various phases of
regression:
Regression Phases in VSO.ai
As we learned in prior sections that VSO.ai enables Smart Stress, Accelerated Coverage,
and Intelligent Exploration phases under the same compute budget as the default
regression, thus yielding a more efficient regression. Various metrics are available to
measure the effectiveness of a VSO.ai regression. An example of a metric for gauging
cost-effectiveness is the cumulative CPU time used to fulfill or surpass the stress,
failure, and coverage metrics of the default regression. The Analytics view provides a
dashboard with a high-level set of comparative metrics is provided to support the claim
of more efficient regressions within the provided compute budget. It helps to measure the
effectiveness of each phase and provides comparisons with the default user regression
(if enabled in compare mode) to build trust in the system. Through these metrics, VSO.ai
aims to provide a comprehensive view of regression effectiveness in comparison with an
unoptimized regression. This comparison allows users to make informed decisions about

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
their verification processes. Raw data is also made available to users to build customized
dashboards.
The high-level metrics are approximations and detailed drill down of coverage
and RTL change information are available in Verdi or URG reports for more
granular insights.
The Analytics dashboard can be invoked at any point after the init step. You have on-
demand access to the live views of analytics. These views enable you to monitor and
analyze the VSO.ai runs during execution, without having to wait for completion.
The following is the summary dashboard for a VSO.ai regression run:
Figure 4 Summary Dashboard for VSO.ai vs Default Regression
Key Terms in the VSO Analytics Dashboard
VSO: All data shown for VSO represents an optimized regression run.

DEF: Represents the default regression run. All data shown for DEF is statistically
estimated unless the compare mode is enabled. In that case, it reflects the actual default
regression metrics.
UI Elements for Coverage Metrics
Figure 5 UI Elements for Coverage Metrics
The following are the UI elements for coverage metrics:
• Instance and Definition selectors show the types of coverage metrics available.
• Code Coverage: Line, Toggle, and FSM coverage. These are enabled only if the
metrics are available in the regression.
• Assertion Coverage: Only enabled if the assertion coverage is available and turned on
in the regression.
• Group Coverage: Enabled if the functional coverage is available.
Graph Controls
• Zoom: Functionality to increase or decrease the viewing scale of the graph for detailed
analysis.
• Reset: Button to revert any user-added changes to the default graph settings.
• Refresh: Button provided on each page shows the current status of the working
directory at that point in time.
Compare Mode – Default vs VSO.ai
The OPT and DEF buttons enable you to compare the standard metrics from the default
regression with optimized metrics generated by VSO.ai. The compare flow must be
enabled for an accurate calculation of the default metrics. Alternatively, a statistical
estimate of regression is shown instead if not in compare mode, providing an approximate
reference.
When activated, this mode overlays the VSO-optimized metrics onto the existing metrics.
This provides a comparison between traditional metrics and AI-enhanced insights.
Opt and Def Buttons

• Default Metrics: Default regression metrics
• VSO Metrics: VSO regression metrics
Progress Chart
The Progress Chart is a line chart that displays the progress over time based on the
various coverage metrics. The metric selector changes the coverage metric displayed.
Figure 6 Total coverage and failure progression

• Tabs:
◦ Zoom and reset options are available for this graph.
◦ The Details button shows the chart data in tabular format for easier analysis.
Figure 7 Tabular View of the Progress Chart

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
• Columns:
◦ X-Axis: Represents the CPU time or the number of runs selected by the toggle
button.
◦ Y-Axis: Represents the coverage percentage (only approximate to URG coverage)
(0% - 100%), for example, "80%".
• Lines:
◦ VSO: Represents progress in the VSO run.
◦ DEF: Represents the estimated progress (actual progress if in compare mode) for
the default run.
◦
Markers on lines: Represent the failure status of the run and shows the number of
failure signatures for the corresponding run.
By default, up to 100 points are plotted on the line. These are adjustable
through --max_markers to ensure a balanced representation without
excessive computation in the estimated flow. For example, if there are 1000
runs, the progress data is generated for every 10th run. A higher marker
count can affect the dashboard generation time as the progress plot must be
computed for each additional marker.
Summarized comparative Metrics
The VSO.ai Analytics dashboard provides a tabular representation of the current metrics.
It compares the VSO and default values. It also shows a gain if the compare mode flow is
enabled.
Figure 8 Summarized Comparative Metrics for Default and VSO.ai Regression Runs

• Columns:
◦ Type:: VSO, DEF (default), or VSO vs DEF (if the compare mode flow is enabled).
◦ CBV Covered #: CBV or Change-Based Verification represents the count of
Covered CBV Targets
◦ CBV Coverage %: Ratio of Covered CBV Targets to total CBV targets
◦ CBV Coverage Efficiency (#/sec): Rate of coverage / CPU time
◦ Coverage Target #: Total coverage targets for the selected metric
◦ Coverage Efficiency (#/sec): Rate of coverage for the the selected metric/CPU
time
◦ Failure Signatures #: Represents the failing runs. clickable failures count provides
the details of failures.
◦ Unique Signatures #: The clickable signatures count provides the details of unique
signatures.
Cards
Figure 9 Cards
The cards in the dashboard are grouped based on their respective categories—Smart
Stress, Convergence, and Intelligent Exploration:
Smart Stress:
The Smart Stress cards shows failure detection in the stress phase, It displays the
following:
• Unique Failure Signatures and Total Failures for VSO and DEF and a difference
measured only in the Smart Stress phase.
• CBV Target Count: The CBV target coverage numbers (measured as the number of
test runs that hit a target), and sorted by histogram buckets by rarity of the CBV target.

• CBV Coverage Count: Same as the metric table CBV Covered #.
• CBV Target Hit Count (by Rarity) | Stress Ratio: This graph depicts the stress ratio.
It measures how much better VSO.ai is at stressing rare events compared to the default
version. The following table explains what the stress ratio scores imply:
Table 2
Score Interpretation
> 1.0 The optimized
version is
better at finding
rare events.
< 1.0 The optimized
version is
worse
The improvements in rare events, (deciles 1-3) score higher than similar
improvements in common events (deciles 8-10).
Figure 10 Stress Ratio
Accelerated Coverage Cards
These cards show the Unique Failure Signatures, Total Failures, Coverage Target Count,
and CBV Coverage Count only in the accelerated coverage phase. The Coverage
Progress Chart is the same as the progress chart, but focusies only on the accelerated
coverage phase.

Intelligent Exploration Cards
These cards show the Unique Failure Signatures, Total Failures for VSO and DEF and a
difference as measured only in the intelligent exploration phase. It also shows Coverage
Target Count, and CBV Coverage Count in this phase. The Coverage Progress Chart is
the same as the progress chart, but focusies only on the accelerated coverage phase.
The Total Target Hit Count (by Rarity) histogram of the coverage targets categorized
by rare to common coverage targets with a visual overlay indicating the difference if the
compare mode is enabled.
These cards analyzes the progress in rare coverage targets (through the histogram of
deciles ordered by rarity of coverage event), providing insights into the depth of coverage
achieved during the Intelligent Exploration phase.

VSO.ai Diagnostics and Advanced Views
The diagnostic capabilities of the VSO.ai Analytics dashboard provide visibility into the
VSO runs, test optimization, coverage tracking, and failure analysis.
In the following sections, this custom document describes the advanced views and
provides the steps to access them:
• Accessing Diagnostics and Advanced Views
• Bin Distributions and Patterns
• Tests Summary and Distribution
• Failure Signatures and Patterns
• Test Runs and Execution Details
Accessing Diagnostics and Advanced Views
To access Diagnostics & Advanced Views, click the Diags button on the navigation bar.
Figure 13 Diagnostics and Advanced Views

Doing so expands or collapses the following advanced diagnostic cards:
Figure 14 Diagnostics and Advanced Views
The cards provides navigation menus for various analytics dashboards.
Bin Distributions and Patterns
The purpose of the Bins group is to provide bin-level analytics and visualizations.
Figure 15 Bins
The following views in the Bins group show bin distributions and patterns:
• Prob Distribution
• Unhit Bins
• Rare Bins
Prob Distribution
The Prob Distribution view is an interactive histogram visualization of probability
distribution. It shows the probability distribution of bins by deciles.
Select a coverage metric to view its probability distribution. You can choose metrics for
group, line, toggle, assertion, or FSM coverage.

Refer to the following screenshot for an example that shows probability distribution for
group definition coverage:
Figure 16 Probability Distribution Histogram - group.def

Unhit Bins
The Unhit Bins view provides a summary of unhit bins for each coverage metric. You can
view a comprehensive list of the uncovered bins for each metric with detailed metadata.
Refer to the following example:
Figure 17 Summary of Unhit Bins
Click an entry in the Number of Unhits column to view the list of unhit bins for a metric.
For example, the following screenshot shows the details of the unhit bins for the fsm.def
coverage metric.
Figure 18 List of Bins

Click an entry in the BIN_Name or BIN_ID to view the comprehensive details of that bin.
The details include the following:
• Metric, bin name, and ID
• Probability values for the selected bin
• Golden seeds suggested for the bin, if any. A golden seed refers to a specific random
seed value that is recommended for a test run. Its purpose is to guide the simulation
toward scenarios that are particularly valuable for verification. These scenarios
include seeds that have previously resulted in failures or are identified as important for
coverage.
• Potential tests that could cover the bin
• Run count of these tests in both the reference and current runs
Figure 19 Bin Summary

Click the current run count of a test to display the following:
• Command-line arguments used in the reference run
Figure 20 Current Test Runs
• Command-line arguments used in the current run

Offline Estimation in VSO.ai
VSO.ai provides the capability to generate a very rough estimate of the expected
VSO.ai gains without having to integrate the VSO.ai steps into the existing regression
environment. Gain estimates are not provided for all VSO.ai value points currently.
Generating an offline estimate with a VDB generated from default regressions
requires a special license that can be obtained by contacting Synopsys
Verification Application Engineers.
Generating an offline estimate requires a complete set of test vdbs from a full regression
run. The following steps are involved in generating the offline estimate.
• Mapping a Test vdb to a Build Name and Test Name
• Building a VSO.ai Model
• Recording Failures
• Estimating Gain
Mapping a Test vdb to a Build Name and Test Name
During the extraction of data from a VDB during the offline estimation step, VSO.ai extracts
all available test paths based on -cm_name and -cm_dir. These paths are extracted
from the VDB directory name or VDB directories list provided using the --vdbdir or --
vdbdirlist option. For example, test paths identified for an example VDB (simv.vdb) are
as follows:
HOST_BASELINE_RH1x1/ts_rnd_tp9_9896
HOST_BASELINE_RH1x2/ts_rnd_tp9_1175
HOST_BASELINE_RH1x2/ts_rnd_tp8_1175
HOST_BASELINE_RH2x1/ts_rnd_tp8_1078
HOST_BASELINE_RH2x1/ts_rnd_tp7_1078
HOST_BASELINE_RH2x2/ts_rnd_tp6_1296
HOST_BASELINE_RH2x2/ts_rnd_tp6_2036
Determining a Build Name
Using --build_regex 'BASELINE_(.*)\/ts' , VSO.ai identifies 4 unique builds, RH1x1,
RH1x2, RH2x1, and RH2x2.

Chapter 5: Offline Estimation in VSO.ai
Building a VSO.ai Model
Determining the Test Template Name
A regular expression containing a group can be provided to VSO.ai using the --
cmname_regex<regex> option. This regular expression is used to match and identify the
test template substring from the cm_name and cm_dir string. Using --cmname_regex
'(ts.*?)_\d+', VSO.ai identifies 4 unique test templates, ts_rnd_tp6,ts_rnd_tp7,
ts_rnd_tp8, and ts_rnd_tp9. --cmname_regex is a regular expression that can be used
to extract the test template name from a test vdb. Alternatively, the --namemap_file
option can be used.
The --namemap file is a tab-separated file, which can either be written by you or
automatically generated using the --test_regex option of VSO.ai to assist in verifying
or adding specific mappings. When the --test_regex option is used, the namemap file is
created in <vso_workdir>/csv/tests_namemap.csv with the following rules:
• All unmatched tests precede the matched tests.
• For all unmatched tests, the test name and build name is NONE. You must review
these and ensure that they are properly filled.
You can use the --test_regex option independently or along with the existing --
cmname_regex/--build_regex option. The mappings specified in the namemap file take
precedence over the mappings derived from the command line --cmname_regex/--
build_regex options.
Building a VSO.ai Model
This stage builds a VSO.ai ML model for offline estimation by using all the test vdbs from
a complete regression run. In addition, VSO.ai needs to be able to map each test vdb to a
corresponding buildname and testname.
To build a model, run the following command:
--vdb2hm \
--vdbdir <path_to_vdb> \
--build_regex <build_regex> \
--cmname_regex <test_regex> \
[grid options] \
[other options]
• --vdb2hm builds the VSO.ai model.
• --vdbdir <input_path_to_vdb> is the path to an input VDB directory. If there are
more than one VDBs, specify the list of VDBs in a text file and pass the file using the
–-vdbdirlist <path_to_file_listing_VDBs> option.

text:
Chapter 5: Offline Estimation in VSO.ai
Recording Failures
• --workdir<workdir> creates the VSO.ai database under <workdir>.
• --build_regex is a regular expression that can be used to extract the build name
from a test vdb. This is not required if there is a single build. Alternatively, the --
namemap_file option can be used.
• --cmname_regex is a regular expression that can be used to extract the test template
name from a test vdb. Alternatively, the --namemap_file option can be used.
• grid_options is a step that is recommended to be run on the grid using the VSO.ai
grid options if there are a large number of test vdbs.
Recording Failures
VSO.ai records the information regarding failing tests (failures) to its database as part
of offline estimation. The test information can be updated in bulk by using the following
--update_fails <csv file> [—update_fails_fmt {cm_name, run_id, batch}] \
--workdir <workdir>
• --update_fails: records all failures specified in <csv file> .
The format of the input CSV file varies based on the --update_fails_fmt option:
◦ cm_name: cm_name, build, PASS/FAIL, signature
◦ run_id: run_id, build, PASS/FAIL, signature
◦ batch: testname, build, nfails, nruns
For the cm_name and run_id formats, the status and signature fields are optional. If
no status is specified, it defaults to fail. The failure signatures are either strings or
numbers.
The following is a sample CSV file using the cm_name format:
1.spi_host_csr_mem_rw_with_rand_reset_8627,bld1,fail,ERR1
1.spe_host_mem_partial_access_19400,bld1,Fail,
2.spi_host_speed_3036,bld1,, 1.spi_host_sw_rest_3196,bld2,,"ERR 2"
• cm_name: is default for coverage-enabled flow (ensuring backward compatibility).
• run_id: is used to update failures in a coverage-enabled flow when the appropriate
option is specified.

Chapter 5: Offline Estimation in VSO.ai
Estimating Gain
It is recommended to use run_id as the fmt for both coverage and no
coverage flow going forward.
• batch: This option replaces the deprecated —update_fails_batch option.
The --update_fails option is not required if the status and failure signatures
for all failing tests are provided during the tell step in the Run stage.
Estimating Gain
VSO.ai estimates the number of runs required on an average to get the same coverage
as the original regression by using the --train option on the model built in the Building
a VSO.ai Model stage. This estimate is not guaranteed but gives an idea of the average
number of test runs needed in a subsequent regression.
To get the estimates of the required runs, execute the following command:
--train \
[other options]
The estimation results are available on stdout as well as in the following VSO.ai work
directory:
<vso_workdir>/train/train.log.

Filtering Target Bins in VSO.ai
VSO.ai supports two mechanisms for filtering the target bins:
• Filtering With Exclusion
• Filtering With HVP
Exclusion is used to specify a hierarchy of bins to be excluded while an Hierarchical
Verification Plan (HVP) plan is used to specify a hierarchy of bins to be included (while the
rest is excluded).
For more details on URG, see the URG section in the VCS User Guide.
Traditionally, the exclusion and HVP plan files can only be applied after the
regression has completed and all the coverage results are available. This is
because functional coverage is of a dynamic nature and the set of all functional
coverage bins cannot be determined until all the runs have been completed.
Therefore, when they are used for filtering in VSO.ai, the target numbers
reported by VSO.ai initially are not going to fully account for all possible
exclusions specified by the exclusion file or HVP plan.
Filtering With Exclusion
The following command can be used to generate an exclusion file from a merged vdb:
urg-dir simv.vdb -dump full_exclusions
The new files are dumped in the directory where you are running. These files contain
excluded objects for the coverage metrics in the commented form. You can copy this file to
a new file, uncomment the objects you want to exclude, and pass the new file to the init
step using the following option:
--elfile <exclusion_file>
Additionally, if multiple exclusion files are to be used, the following option can be passed to
the init step instead of the --elfile option:
--elfilelist <exclusion_file_list>

Chapter 6: Filtering Target Bins in VSO.ai
Filtering With HVP
exclusion_file_list: is the file containing a list of exclusion file paths, one per line.
• In addition to providing the exclusion file option, you must specify the path for all the
build simv files either by specifying the simv_location in the configuration file or by
using -–simv_paths/--simv_path_list command line option. Alternately, you can
also specify comp_vdb_path in the configuration file to specify the compile VDB path
for each of the builds.
• The -–simv_paths/--simv_path_list option or comp_vdb_path field is not required
if only functional coverage is being used and required if any code coverage metric is
being used as part of the targeted metrics.
The above two methods apply for both --elfile/--elfilelist and --plan options.
For more information, refer to section Appendix D: Configuration File.
Filtering With HVP
Bin filtering can also be done using an HVP plan. VSO.ai supports both a plan file and a
server based HVP plan. As in exclusions, you need to specify the paths for all the build
simv files if any code coverage metric is being used.
The HVP plan file can be specified at the init step using the following option:
--plan <hvp_plan_file>
Additionally, the server plan can be specified using the following options:
--hvp_server <HVP_SERVER> \
--hvp_proj <HVP_PROJ> \
--plan <PLAN_NAME>
--mod <MODIFIER_FILE>

following considerations should be noted:
• Scores matches for assert and FSM.
• For Tgl, scores matches when URG report is generated with -portsonly.
• Line and Group numbers differs.

Line coverage (line/block coverage) in VCS measures: Whether each executable line
or statement block in the RTL/code is executed at least once during simulation.
A block is essentially:
◦ A group of statements treated as one execution unit
◦ Typically corresponds to:
▪ begin end
▪ procedural blocks (always, initial)
▪ single-line statements
For example,
always @(posedge clk) begin
if (en) begin
y <= a + b;
end
end
Coverage breakdown:
◦ always block → 1 block
◦ if (en) condition → condition coverage (separate metric)
◦ y <= a + b; → a line/block to be executed

Cloud/Remote Mode in VSO.ai
This section details the use model changes required to deploy VSO.ai on cloud or support
multiple data centers where NFS is not available. These changes are to enable support for
both hybrid and cloud-only environments. In a cloud-only environment, VSO.ai supports
object storage for VSO.ai ML models, thereby removing any requirement of having
access to the NFS type storage. In a hybrid mode, VSO.ai supports both cloud and local
compute. It also supports object storage to share content between the on-prem and cloud
deployments.
The cloud mode leverages object/blob storage as a way for the simulation jobs to
communicate with the VSO.ai work directory. In addition, it also provides the ability to store
the ML directory (dbdir) in the object/blob storage.
Authentication to object/blob storage is supported using the rclone configuration file.
The following are the changes required in each of the VSO.ai steps to use the cloud:
1. Configure the remote storage:
a. If using rclone:
Generate a configuration file, rclone, that contains the access credentials for
object/blob storage. The rclone configuration file can be generated by running the
following command and following the prompts:
$VSO_HOME/linux64/bin/rclone config
See https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_config/ for more information on the rclone
config.
Since rclone also supports the ability to synchronize data using sftp, the rclone
configuration file generated with sftp as the remote type can be used with VSO.ai
across multiple data centers. The rest of this section does not distinguish between
the type of the remote configured in the rclone configuration file.
The following syntax is used to specify the remote object/blob storage location:
<rclone_config_path>:<rclone_name>:<subdir>

Chapter 7: Cloud/Remote Mode in VSO.ai

▪ rclone_config_path is the full path to the rclone configuration file generated
using the rclone config command.
▪ rclone_name is the remote name defined in the rclone configuration file.
▪ subdir is a subdirectory within the object/blob storage under which to store the
VSO.ai data.
b. If using gcloud:
VSO.ai assumes that the authentication in this case is handled by gcloud, either
through the gcloud configuration file or through a service account attached to a
VM. In this case, the following syntax is used to specify the remote object/blob
storage location:
gs://:<bucket_name>/<sub_directory>
Additionally, the following VSO.ai init step option would be required:
--remote_sync_cmd gcloud
c. If using aws:
VSO.ai assumes that the authentication in this case is handled by aws, either
through the aws configuration file or through the appropriate role attached to a VM.
In this case, the following syntax is used to specify the remote object/blob storage
location:
s3://:<bucket_name>/<sub_directory>
Additionally, the following VSO.ai init step option would be required:
--remote_sync_cmd aws
2. If a dbdir directory is already available locally and it needs to be moved to object/blob
storage, the following command can be executed in the on-prem environment where
access to dbdir is available:
--merge \
--out <remote_dbdir>

Chapter 7: Cloud/Remote Mode in VSO.ai

◦ dbdir is the path to the local dbdir.
◦ workdir is the path to an empty local workdir because merge needs two
directories
◦ remote_dbdir is the remote object/blob storage path specified here using the
format as described in step 1.
3. Init Step:
To prepare a new VSO.ai work directory using dbdir as reference, the init command
is used as follows:
--init \
--workdir <local_workdir> \
--remote_workdir <remote_workdir> \
--dbdir <local_or_remote_dbdir> \
[--remote_sync_cmd <path_to_rclone_override>] \
[other options]
◦ local_workdir is the path to the work directory on the local file system or NFS.
All VSO.ai steps except the simulation job must have access to this local work
directory.
◦ remote_workdir is a temporary work directory in the object/blob storage that
VSO.ai uses to communicate data to/from the simulation job that is run on the
cloud. The remote work directory path is specified using the format as described in
step 2.
◦ local_or_remote_dbdir is the dbdir that can either be on the local disk/NFS or
on the object/blob storage. If it is on local storage, a normal Unix type path is used.
If it is in object/blob storage, then the path is specified using the format describe in
step 2.
◦ --remote_sync_cmd is optionally used to override the default rclone utility that
VSO.ai uses to synchronize data to/from the remote cloud storage. VSO.ai has
native support to use gcloudor aws instead of rclone. If the user wishes to use any
other tool, this overridden utility must support similar options as what the standard
rclone utility uses. It must support the following rclone subcommands: sync,

Chapter 7: Cloud/Remote Mode in VSO.ai

purge, and delete. Additionally, it must support the rclone--config option with
similar configuration file syntax.
For the first VSO.ai run (that is Day0), there might be no dbdir available.
Therefore, the --dbdir option is not specified.
4. Ask Step:
The ask step in VSO.ai needs access to the local work directory from above. That
means that the ask command must be run on a host that has access to this local work
directory. No additional changes are necessary to the ask command in the cloud mode.
The ask command is as follows:
--ask \
--workdir <local_workdir> \
[other ask options]
5. Execute Step:
The next step after the ask is to run the tests as predicted by the ask step. These tests
can either be run on-prem or on the cloud.
If they are run on-prem, then no changes are necessary for the cloud mode for those
specific runs. The vso_workdir passed to the simv file in that case would be the
path to the local work directory.

can either be run on-prem or on the cloud.
If they are run on-prem, then no changes are necessary for the cloud mode for those
specific runs. The vso_workdir passed to the simv file in that case would be the
path to the local work directory. The following command line is used for an on-prem
simulation job:
simv \
-vso_opts workdir=<local_workdir> \
-vso_opts run_id=<run_id> \
[other options]
If the simulation job is run on the cloud instead, it requires access to both a temporary
local disk and the object/blob storage.
simv \
-vso_opts workdir=<local_temp_path> \
-vso_opts run_id=<run_id> \
[-vso_opts remote_workdir=<remote_workdir>] \
[-vso_opts remote_sync_cmd=<rclone_override>] \
[other simv options]
◦ local_temp_path is a temporary path on the local file system that is accessible
to the simv file. This is used by the simv file to temporarily store data that it has
downloaded from object/blob storage. This directory must exist.

Chapter 7: Cloud/Remote Mode in VSO.ai

To support older VCS versions, the additional remote work directory path should be
specified using an environment variable.
export VSO_REMOTE_WORKDIR=<remote_workdir>
Additionally, to override the rclone command in the older VCS versions, the following
environment variable can be used:
export VSO_REMOTE_SYNC_CMD=<rclone_override>
6. Tell Step
The tell step in VSO.ai needs access to the local work directory from above. That
means that the tell command must be run on a host that has access to this local work
directory. No additional changes are necessary to the tell command in the cloud mode.
The tell command is as follows:
--tell <run_id> \
--workdir <local_workdir> \
[other tell options]
7. Finalize Step
After all the regression runs have completed, the finalize step is invoked. The
finalize step in VSO.ai needs access to the local work directory from above. That
means that the finalize command must be run on a host that has access to this local
work directory. No additional changes are necessary to the finalize command in the
cloud mode. The finalize command is as follows:
--finalize \
--workdir <local_workdir> \
[other finalize options]
8. Merge Step
The final step involves merging the results of this regression into the common ML
directory (dbdir). As discussed earlier, VSO.ai supports either a local dbdiror a
remote dbdir stored on object/blob storage. The merge step needs access to the local
work directory from above. That means that the merge command must be run on a
host that has access to this local work directory. The merge command is as follows:
--merge \
--workdir <local_workdir> \
--dbdir <local_or_remote_dbdir>
If dbdir is on local storage, then a normal Unix type path is used. If it is in object/blob
storage, the path is specified using the format describe in step 2 above.

Compare Mode in VSO.ai
This section describes the capability of VSO.ai to compare the coverage and failure results
of a VSO.ai regression with a parallel regression that does not use VSO.ai. An additional
requirement is that you should be able to achieve this comparison by following the same
existing VSO.ai use model. This provides a consistent way to compare the results of
VSO.ai across multiple designs.
The following are the changes required in the VSO.ai steps to use the compare mode:
1. Init Step
To initialize a new VSO.ai work directory in compare mode using dbdir as reference,
use the init command as follows:
--init \
--compare \
--regr_config <config_file> \
[other options]
• --compare enables the compare mode.
• config_file is the VSO.ai configuration file in the YAML format.
The config_file is necessary to provide the following information to VSO.ai:
• Builds that should be enabled
• Tests that should be run
• Number of times each test should be performed. This is done by specifying the count
attribute in the configuration file.

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
In the compare mode, the following changes occur at each step:
1. Init Step:
VSO.ai creates two subdirectories under the user specified work directory when the
init call is made. One is used for the default run and the other is used for the VSO.ai
run.
You do not need to do any special handling of these subdirectories. Only the top-level
work directory needs to be specified for all commands. VSO.ai automatically infers the
work directory that must be used for each command.
VSO.ai invokes the init command under each of these work directories.
2. Ask/Tell Step:
VSO.ai first uses the VSO work directory to identify all the tests to be run in the flow
and returns these as part of the ask result. After all the VSO run tests have been
provided, VSO.ai switches to providing tests from the default run.
VSO.ai automatically infers the run (default or VSO) that each tell corresponds to
(using the run_id).
You do not need to distinguish that the run is part of the default run or the VSO run.
3. Finalize Step:
VSO.ai invokes finalize under each work directory when the finalize call is made by the
user.
This step generates three reports. The first report is the default work directory that
contains the results of the default regression. The second report is in the VSO work
directory that contains the results of the VSO regression run and its comparison with
the Day 0 run. The third report is the top-level work directory that contains a report
comparing the VSO.ai run with the default run.
The exit conditions for each run are as follows:
• The default run stops after a limit is reached for each test provided using the count
attribute in the configuration file.
• The VSO.ai run stops after it has exceeded the total amount of compute time expected
to be taken by the default run. This terminating condition can be controlled using the –-
exit and –-phase VSO.ai options.

text:
Verdi VMS Integration with VSO.ai
This chapter explains the VSO.ai plug-in that enables a seamless integration of the
VSO.ai Regression Optimization engine in Verdi VMS administered regressions. When
users enable the VSO.ai plug-in, Verdi VMS automatically gathers and manages the
AI/ML-driven test selections of VSO.ai. This process accelerates the achievement of
expected coverage with fewer test runs, thereby enhancing regression grid efficiency and
maximizing coverage return on investment (ROI).
This chapter comprises the following sections:
• Installation of the VSO.ai Regression Optimizer Plug-In
• Workflow
• Use Model
• Options for VSO.ai Driver and Plug-in
• Input and Output Directories
• Step-Specific Options for VSO.ai Plug-in
• Running VSO Steps on the Grid
Installation of the VSO.ai Regression Optimizer Plug-In
This section explains the prerequisites and the steps for the installation of the VSO.ai plug-
in in Verdi VMS.

Installation of the VSO.ai Regression Optimizer Plug-In
Prerequisites
Before using the VSO.ai Regression Optimizer plug-in, ensure that the following
prerequisites are completed:
• VMS and VSO.ai are installed. VMS and VSO.ai are available as part of VCS
installation. If your setup requires separate installation, follow the appropriate steps to
install them individually.
• Verdi VMS database and web servers are running.
• Coverage is enabled. To enable Coverage in ExecMan use either of the command line
options: -merge_cov_dir or -merge_dir.
VSO.ai can optimize regression tests based on the following:
• Code metrics, such as Line, FSM, Toggle, and Assert
• Functional coverage metrics, such as Group
To enable VSO.ai to learn and optimize regressions for specific coverage types, activate
the required coverage metrics during VCS compilation and simulation.
By default, VSO-enabled ExecMan sessions automatically create the VSO ML model (also
known as the VSO workdir) at the following location:
../depot/cvsdepot/<user>/<project>/<config>/<session>/vso_workdir
To create the VSO workdir in the spool area rather than the depot area, set
the environment variable SHOW_UNIFIED_HIER_IN_POST_INSTALL 1 before
you start the ExecMan post installation. Alternatively, you can add a username
layer to the VSO workdir in the spool area by setting the environment variable
EMAN_UNIFIED_FOLDER_HIER_USER to 1.
Installation of VSO.ai Plug-in in Verdi VMS
To install and use the plug-in with Verdi VMS, perform the following steps:
1. Copy the synopsys_eman.setup file from ExecMan installation directory to your local
directory. Then, update the file with the following content:
- vso: $VSO_HOME/plugin/eman/vso_v2.pyc
2. Update the configuration (.emc) file with the following content:
- vso

Workflow
3. Set up the Verdi VMS project and its environment variable using the following
commands:
source <EMAN_INSTALL>/VMS/bin/sourceme.csh

eman project create <project_name>

setenv VMS_PROJECT <project_name>

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
setenv EMAN_SETUP_FILE <your_path_to_synopsys_eman.setup>
// This is required as you cannot modify the central
synopsys_eman.setup.
Workflow
The VSO.ai machine learning model analyzes the association between tests, number
of runs, and coverage achieved from coverage VDBs of ExecMan regressions. The
initial regression enabled by VSO.ai serves as a learning regression, during which no
optimizations are performed. Subsequent regressions are optimized by VSO.ai to achieve
the enabled regression goals.
The following are some regression-based verification goals that VSO.ai helps improve:
• Targeting potential and known failures
• Stress validation of changes in the design
• Accelerating expected coverage achievement
• Enhancing coverage through exploration
ExecMan collaborates with the VSO.ai plug-in to deliver a seamless experience for VSO.ai
optimized regressions. When preparing to initiate a regression, ExecMan interacts with
the plug-in to obtain recommended tests for the session—whether it is the initial run or a
later iteration—through ASK procedure. Using ASK, you can access rank-ordered tests
recommended by the VSO.ai ML model for the regression. ExecMan executes these tests
on the designated regression compute farm and automates VSO.ai-specific options to
extract learning metadata from the test run VDBs.
Additionally, the TELL procedure allows VSO.ai to learn dynamically during the first run or
reinforce existing learnings during subsequent runs. The automated interaction between
ExecMan and the VSO.ai plug-in simplifies the ASK-RUN-TELL workflow, enhancing
compute grid efficiency.

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
Workflow
The following figure shows the train with N-ask and N-tell steps:
Day 0 or Init:
The first run with the plug-in is called a VSO.ai initialization run. In this run, the tests are
not optimized. Rather, the metadata about all tests, which are being run on the first run,
are collected.
This is the most important run to construct the VSO.ai model and train on it.
VSO.ai plug-in automatically detects the user area whether it is first run or subsequent run
and accordingly collects data.
Day N or Optimized:
After the initial run, the VSO.ai plug-in searches through previous Verdi VMS sessions to
see whether a model is already available. When it finds one, it uses the insights gained
from that model and performs an optimized run using VSO.ai optimization methods.
If seeds are specified in the .emc file, they are considered in the initial run but later the
seeds are dependent on the VSO.ai plug-in.

Use Model
Use Model
This section shows the use model of Verdi VMS-VSO.ai plug-in. This use model is
categorized into the following sections:
Setup
To install and start using the VSO.ai plug-in in Verdi VMS, see the Installation of the
VSO.ai Regression Optimizer Plug-In.
Init
After the VSO.ai plug-in is enabled, the plug-in checks the user area (that is, Verdi VMS
project/config cvsdepot) to find any preexisting VSO.ai model.
If no model is found, VSO.ai plug-in automatically runs in the init mode and creates the
first model. No extra options are needed. For example:
eman -regr_config my_config.emc
The VSO.ai plug-in populates the two environment variables provided in the
following table for compile time and runtime. These variables have settings for
VSO.ai to collect the correct metadata for the model. You need to ensure that
these variables are used appropriately.
Compile (vcs) SNPS_VSO_COMPILE_ARGS vcs ${SNPS_VSO_COMPILE_ARGS} -cm …
Runtime
(simv)
SNPS_VSO_RUNTIME_ARGS simv ${SNPS_VSO_RUNTIME_ARGS} -cm …
To set the number of tests required in the initial ask, use the following variable:
EMAN_INITIAL_SCHEDULE_TESTS_COUNT
The default value is twice the number of nodes. This variable controls the number of test
runs (ASK) that the plug-in requests from the VSO.ai model during the initial regression.
To set the number of incremental asks, use the following variable:
EMAN_INCR_TEST_COUNT
The default value is 1.
An incremental ask involves completing a few tests before proceeding to request
additional ones. When you specify the number of incremental asks, the VSO.ai plug-in
ensures that the current test is completed before initiating the next one. This approach
enhances the quality of the ask but results in longer processing times, and the grid
resources are not used to their full capacity.

Use Model
When configuring regression runs, it is important to consider the type of regression and
set the environment variables accordingly. For instance, a Gatekeeper regression run
may prioritize throughput and quick results, where a slight reduction in GAINs might be
acceptable. In contrast, nightly or volume runs can leverage the additional time to optimize
for GAIN performance. Additionally, a single ASK can be used to provide all the required
tests for secure, comprehensive coverage at the start of a regression session. This is
achieved using the VSO.ai plug-in options in the ExecMan command line.
For example:
eman -regr_config my_config.emc -plugin_options "vso -ask all"
Run
After the VSO.ai model is created, the VSO.ai plug-in performs an offline estimate to figure
out the optimized number of runs needed to reach the same coverage. The plug-in goes
through a similar search process under the Verdi VMS cvsdepot (project/config) to find
any preexisting model and if found, it runs the optimized number of tests based on offline
estimate. Note that there is no change in the command line for Verdi VMS.
For example:
eman -regr_config my_config.emc
Reset/Force Init
You can initialize the model forcefully using the following -plugin_options option:
eman -regr_config my_config.emc -plugin_options "vso -init"
Disable
To disable the plug-in and run ExecMan, you can either comment out the plugins block in
the .emc file or use the command line option, -disable_plugins vso as follows:
eman -regr_config my_config.emc -disable_plugins vso
VSO-Specific Options
To send options specific to VSO.ai during a Verdi VMS run, you can use the following
format:
eman -regr_config my_config.emc -plugin_options "vso [options]"
For the list of options, see Options for VSO.ai Driver and Plug-in.
Adding Tests
To add a test, you need to simply add the test in the Verdi VMS .emc configuration file.
VSO.ai parses the Verdi VMS configuration file during every run to determine if new tests
are added and runs all of them, by default, without any optimization. For more information

Options for VSO.ai Driver and Plug-in
on how to add tests in the ExecMan configuration file, see the VC Execution Manager
Configuration File chapter.
Removing Tests
To remove tests, you need to remove the tests from the .emc file. The VSO.ai plug-in
automatically detects the test removal by loading the last VSO.ai model and by comparing
with the current snapshot of the .emc file. After a removed test is detected, offline
estimates automatically stop suggesting the test.
Changing Tests
Changing the name of a test is considered as the removal of the old test name and
addition of a new one. The first run occurs without any optimization. The new test is
optimized starting with the subsequent runs.
Options for VSO.ai Driver and Plug-in
This section describes the options that are for the VSO.ai driver and the options that are
consumed in the plug-in. These options are added to the command line.
• VSO.ai Driver Options:
To use VSO.ai options with plug-in, use the following syntax:
-plugin_options "vso [options]"
The following are the VSO.ai driver options:

You can also use the following tests budgeting option through ExecMan
arguments to control the test size.
% eman … -tests_budget_num 10 Where, 10 is the maximum number of

Input and Output Directories
The VSO.ai model is stored under cvsodepot of ExecMan.
../depot/cvsdepot/<user>/<project>/<config>/<session>/vso_workdir
The vso_workdir contains all the data that VSO tracks.
The following are the important directories under vso_workdir:
• vso_workdir/eman: Contains the vso.log plug-in log file, which has the summary of
each VSO.ai driver step, such as init, ask, tell, finalize, and so on.
• vso_workdir/online: Contains the VSO online model directory.
• vso_workdir/hm: Contains the VSO specific data.
• vso_workdir/info: Contains the coverage information.
• vso_workdir/train: Contains the offline training estimate.
• vso_workdir/report: Contains the report generated by the current run.

Step-Specific Options for VSO.ai Plug-in
VSO.ai report is located under the Session Attributes page of Verdi VMS:
<cvsdepot>/…/<session>/vso_workdir/report/index.html
• vso_workdir/profile: Contains the profile output for all the commands executed by
VSO.
In the secure mode of Verdi VMS, the cvsdepot is stored under the spool area.
While the top-level directory structure varies up to vso_workdir, the structure
within vso_workdir remains consistent.
Step-Specific Options for VSO.ai Plug-in
You can define step-specific options for the VSO plug-in in the .emc file. These options
provide granular control over each step in the VSO process such as init, ask, tell, train,
finalize, and merge.
You can replace the <step>_opts placeholder with the following step-specific option:
• init: Options for the initialization step.
• ask: Options for the query or ask step.
• tell: Options for updating information.
• train: Options for the estimation/training step.
• finalize: Options for the finalization step.
• merge: Options for merging data or results.
• default: Options for all steps.
Priority Between Command Line and EMC File Options
When both command line and .emc file options are specified for a VSO step, the following
priority rules apply:
• If a command line option is specified, it overrides the corresponding step option defined
in the .emc file.
• If a command line option is not provided, then the .emc file option is used.
EMC file option

Determining the vso_workdir Directory
By default, ExecMan creates a vso_workdir for each regression session in the cvsdepot
path assigned to that session.
To change the default location, you can specify the preferred path in the .emc file.
Determining the vso_dbdir Directory
For VSO enabled regression runs that are not marked as a Day0 runs (using the -init
option), ExecMan searches for the vso_workdir from the most recent completed session
that matches the current project's configuration.
If a match is found, ExecMan selects that vso_workdir as the dbdir (parent session) for
the current run.
To specify a different dbdir, you can use one of two ways:
• Update the .emc file.
• Use the command line option:
% vms -plugin_options "vso -parent_session <name of previous
session with a vso_workdir>"
If the specified session is not found, or if the session is found but does not
have a .done marker indicating completion, then ExecMan cannot use it as the
parent session.
Merge
To merge the data with the directory, set the merge_into_dbdir option as follows:
• merge_into_dbdir: true : To merge data into the central database directory.
• merge_into_dbdir: false : To merge data into the vso_workdir of the current
session.
Set the vso_dbdir option to define the central path for the database directory. If you do
not specify vso_dbdir, VSO uses the default path, which is cvsdepot.
vso_dbdir: <central path> | optional => default: cvsdepot

Running VSO Steps on the Grid
Set the merge_into_dbdir option to true to enable merging into the central database
directory. By default, this option is set to false, and merging occurs only in the current
session.
merge_into_dbdir: true | false | optional => default: false
EMC file
- vso:
# General options for VSO
init_opts: -target_covered_percentage 0.9
finalize_opts: -prune
default_opts: -nprocesses 2

# Directory management options
vso_dbdir: </path/to/dbdir>
vso_workdir: </path/to/workdir>
merge_into_dbdir: true
All the step-specific options should be specified under plugins -> vso.
Running VSO Steps on the Grid
To run the VSO steps on the grid, set up the configure file and the execution behavior.
Setting Up the Configuration File
To configure the grid options for sending a VSO step to the grid, follow these steps:
1. Define the grid_opt under the required plug-in in the configuration file.
2. Specify the appropriate grid in the synopsys.setup file.
grid_opts_setup:
- init_opt: run -D -forcelog -F -l init.log
- end_opt: run -D -forcelog -F -l end.log
- vso:
grid_opt:
init_block: init_opt
end_block: end_opt
timeout: 300

Running VSO Steps on the Grid
Execution Behavior
The execution of the configuration file is as follows:
• init_block: Grid options for sending the VSO init step to the grid.
• end_block: Grid options for sending the VSO finalize, merge, and train steps
to the grid. These steps run one after another on the same grid machine instead of
running independently on different grid machines.
• If local_host is specified, the plug-in function executes locally.
• If no grid_opt is specified, plug-in functions run as part of the main eman process.

text:
--detect_stale Enable the detection of stale bins at runtime. This has a simulation-time
performance impact.
--
dump_total_targ
ets
Track and display the count of all covered and uncovered bins. This
significantly degrades the performance of VSO.ai.
--exit {fails:F,
runs:R,
cpu[:C[X]]}
Additional overrides to terminate the regression run. By default, the exit
condition is determined based on the phases selected by –-phase. The
overriding condition values are fails:F. Ask returns no test if there have
been F failures.
runs:R Ask does not return more than R number of tests runs.
cpu:C Ask limits the number of runs to not exceed more than C hours
of estimated run time cpu:CX. Ask limits the number of runs so that the
estimated total run time does not exceed C times the total run time of the
default regression.
More than one condition can be specified by either using a comma separated
list or repeating the –-exit option.
--ignore_failed Do not consider coverage from failed tests. By default, VSO.ai includes the
coverage from failed tests in determining the exit condition and for targeting
purposes.
--
min_runs_per_t
est N
The minimum number of times each of the tests should be run even if VSO.ai
determines that the test should be run for a fewer number of times to achieve
the target.
--no_vdb_merge Do not merge the vdbs during the online run. VSO.ai automatically merges
the vdbs using the union merge option as part of the online flow. This merged
vdb can then be used to view the coverage report and for generating any
exclusions for the next regression run.
--
phase{stress[:
N],
acceleration,
exploration}
List of phases to target. Values are stress[:N], acceleration, and
exploration.
More than one phase can be selected by either using a comma separated list
of repeating the --phase option.
--pre_init
COMMAND_STRING
Execute COMMAND_STRING at the start of the init step. Specified as a Unix
command with arguments in quotes.
--post_init
COMMAND_STRING
Execute COMMAND_STRING at the end of the init step. Specified as a Unix
command with arguments in quotes.
--project
PROJECT
The name of the project this regression belongs to. The project name is used
to segregate data on a per project level in the dbdir and to also show a per
project level visualization of results.
--regr_config
VSO.ai configuration file in the YAML format. Refer to the appendix section
for more details on the configuration file.

title: Version Y-2026.03-SP1, June 2026
text:
--
remote_sync_comm
and CMD
Override the rclone command used by VSO.ai to perform data
synchronization in the cloud mode.
--remote_workdir
REMOTE_PATH
Remote workdir for the VSO run. Used for passing information between
the local workdir and the remote/cloud simulation jobs. If access
credentials are required, then the workdir path is specified as follows:
<path_to_rclone_config>:<rclone_name>:<remote_path>
If access credentials are not required, the workdir path can be specified as
the object/blob store path. Refer to the Cloud Mode chapter for more details
on the cloud mode.
--simv_paths
PATH_LIST
A list of comma-separated paths to all the build simv files targeted by the
current regression run. It can also be specified by using the configuration file
in –-regr_config or in a file with –-simv_path_list.
--simv_path_list
List of the simv paths pf builds specified in a file, one line per simv.
--skip_vdb Skip processing the vdb at the end of the simulation. Instead, the vdb is
passed to the tell step for processing.
--
target_covered_p
ercentage
PERCENT
Target a specific percentage of the covered bins from the reference during
the Acceleration phase. Value is from 0.0 to 1.0. The default value is 1.0
(100%).
--user USERNAME The user this regression run should be attributed to. By default, the Unix
USER environment variable is used. The username is used to segregate data
on a per user level and to also show a per user level visualization of results.
Init Step and Offline Configuration Options
--elfile
Exclusion file to apply for targeting.
--elfilelist
List of exclusion files to apply for targeting.
--fsm {state,
transition,
state+transiti
on}
Select the FSM coverage metrics to target: state or transition.
By default, FSM transitions are extracted and targeted. Only a subset can be
extracted by using the following options:
• --fsmstate: Extracts or targets only states
• --fsmtransition: Extracts or targets only transitions.
• --fsmstate+transition: Extracts or targets both states and transitions.
--hvp_proj
PROJECT_NAME
Used in conjunction with –-hvp_server and –-plan to filter bins.

--hvp_server
SERVER_URL
Used in conjunction with –-hvp_proj and –-plan to filter bins.
--mod
<modifier_file>
Enables you to dynamically filter and modify HVP coverage features using
external modifier files, providing fine-grained control over which coverage
elements are included in CSO optimization.
--plan
<hvp_plan_file>
Enables filtering with HVP bin filtering using an HVP plan.
--
ignore_testlist
Specifies a file containing the list of tests to be ignored, where each test is
specified as test_name@@build_name.
--no_show_ratios Do not use show_ratios weights. By default, the show_ratios weights are
used.
--plan FILENAME The HVP plan file to use to filter the bins for targeting
.
--target_metric
{all, assert,
cond, fsm,
group, line,
tgl}
A comma separates list of metrics to target.
For a metric to be targeted by VSO.ai in a regression run, it has to be
enabled during the VCS compile step. Also, the ML model for the metric must
exist.
--tgl
{portsonly, all}
Select the toggle coverage metrics to target.
Ask Step Options
--fmt {csv,
json, shell}
Output format for –-ask --out . The default is csv format.
--simstats Get the estimated peak memory in the --ask output.
Tell Step Options
--failed
[SIGNATURE]
The run corresponding to the specific tell has failed. The failure signature
can be provided using SIGNATURE. Multiple signatures can be specified by
repeating the –-failure option.
Finalize Step Options
--prune Clean up the workdir after finalize.
Report Step Options (Also apply to Finalize Step)
--reportdir
DIRNAME
Store the generated report in REPORTDIR. By default, the report is in
WORKDIR/report.

Merge Step Options
--dbdir DIRNAME Merges the learning from workdir with the learning inside DIRNAME. Unless
–-out is specified, the result is stored into DIRNAME.
Offline Estimation Options
--build_regex
REGEX
Regex with groups representing a build for extracting the build names from
the vdb path.
--cmname_regex
REGEX
Regex with groups representing tests in cmname for extracting test names.
--namemap
Path to the file containing mapping from the test path to the test and build
name.
--test_regex
Validates cmname_regex, build_regex and dumps the matched and
unmatched tests. Dumps to FILENAME if specified or to stdout, if the file name
is not specified.
--urg_merge_opts
OPTS
Additional URG options passed to the URG merge during the vdb2hm step.
--vdbdir DIRNAME The path to VDB directories for the vdb2hm step.
--vdbdirlist
The list of VDB directories in a file for the vdb2hm step
.
Grid and Parallel Job Options
--
grid_default_o
pts DEFAULT_OPTS
For lsf, VSO.ai internally adds -cwd <pwd> . For uge, VSO.ai internally adds
-cwd -V . Use this option to override the internally added grid options).
--grid_opts OPTS Additional grid options to choose the right machine configuration.
--
grid_status_cmd
CMD
The grid command to be used to check the status of a job.
--grid_type
{lsf, uge}
The type of grid being used.
--maxjobsN Maximum number of parallel jobs that can be submitted to the grid.
--nprocessesN Specify the number of processors to use in parallel on the host machine.
--sub{qsub,
bsub}
Grid Submit command.
Other Options

Appendix B: New Options
--
disable_version_
check
Disable the version mismatch check. This is not recommended.
--file FILENAME Load arguments from file.
-h, --help Show help message with options and exits.
--licqueue Wait for the license if all licenses are checked out by other jobs.
--print_selected Print the list of selected tests/seeds in each ask.
--timestamp Add timestamps and file information to the log files.
--version
[{short, full}]
Print version and exit.

The following table shows the newly introduced VSO.ai options.
New Option Description
--analytics Start the server to view the analytics report in a browser.

VSO --regr_config Reference
The --regr_config option uses a YAML configuration file that defines tests, builds, and
the relationships of tests and builds for the VSO online flow. This configuration file lists the
tests to run and the options for each test. For more information on the file format and on
options in the builds and tests blocks, see the VC Execution Manager Configuration File
chapter in the VC Execution Manager User Guide.
This file is essential for:
• Defining test names and their associated builds
• Specifying run counts (min, max, default)
• Configuring simulation arguments
• Setting up simv locations for each build
• Defining optuner parameters for hyperparameter optimization
The configuration is required for most operations, including --init, --ask, --
tell, --finalize, and --run_checks.
File Format
The configuration uses YAML format with support for:
• Environment variable expansion: $VAR or ${VAR}
• Custom variable expansion: Variables defined in the variables section
• Special placeholders: $${EMAN_RANDOM} for random seed injection
To assist you in writing the configuration, VSO.ai provides a helper utility to generate the
configuration file template (in YAML format) from the existing VSO.ai learning database.
You can use the file cfg_file as a starting point to define the regression test list:
$VSO_HOME/bin/driver --gencfg --out <cfg_file> --workdir <vso_dbdir>

--gencfg runs the configuration generator to generate a configuration file for VSO.ai
based on a workdir created from either the vdb2hm step or a full VSO.ai regression.
This command is only needed when a new configuration file template needs to be
(re)generated. The corresponding runtime arguments of each test template are populated
automatically as follows:
- name: test_r8_w8_r4_w4
build: cfg1
arguments: -vso cso -lca -vso_opts testname=test_r8_w8_r4_w4
-cm_name test_r8_w8_r4_w4_$${EMAN_RANDOM}
+UVM_TESTNAME=test_r8_w8_r4_w4 +ntb_random_seed=$${EMAN_RANDOM}
${common_opts}

- name: test_2m_4s
build: cfg2
arguments: -vso cso -lca -vso_opts testname=test_2m_4s
-cm_name test_2m_4s_$${EMAN_RANDOM} +UVM_TESTNAME=test_2m_4s
+ntb_random_seed=$${EMAN_RANDOM} ${common_opts}

- name: test_read_modify_write
build: cfg2
arguments: -vso cso -lca -vso_opts
testname=test_read_modify_write -cm_name
test_read_modify_write_$${EMAN_RANDOM}
+UVM_TESTNAME=test_read_modify_write +ntb_random_seed=$${EMAN_RANDOM}
${common_opts}
When you use the Wrapper interface instead of the Ask-Tell interface, runtime
arguments for a predicted test come from the configuration file. The arguments
field for each test must be non-empty in that mode.
You can also run a script before the init step—for example, to read an existing test list,
emit a VSO.ai YAML configuration file, and pass that file to --regr_config.
--init
--pre_init gen_script.py customer_test.lst new_config.yaml \
--regr_config new_config.yaml
• --pre_init is a defined place to connect the user script before the init step.
• gen_script.py is a script name created by the user for conversion.

• customer_test.lst is a file list which list builds, tests and the number of seeds and
so on.
• new_config.yaml is an output YAML file name after the conversion to be used during
the init step.

Relationship Between Tests and Builds
Tests reference builds through the build field:
• A test can specify a single build: build: bld1
• A test can specify multiple builds (comma-separated): build: bld1, bld2
• If no build is specified, the test uses "default" as the build name
• The build name in tests creates an implicit build entry if not defined in builds section

Variables Section
The variables section allows you to define custom variables that can be referenced
elsewhere in the configuration using ${variable_name} syntax.
Structure
The following is the variable structure:
- var1: value1
- var2: value2
- complex_var: ${var1}/subdir/${var2}
Processing Order
The following are the processing steps:
1. Environment variables ($VAR) are expanded first.
2. YAML is parsed to extract the variables section.
3. Variables are temporarily added to the environment.
4. All ${var} references are expanded.
5. Final YAML is parsed with all expansions complete.

If a variable is null or not defined, expansion treats it as an empty string.
The following is the example for variables section:
- vcs: $VCS_HOME/bin/vcs
- current_dir: $PWD
- common_opts: -cm line+assert+fsm+tgl
- simv_base: ${current_dir}/build

simv_location: ${simv_base}/simv # Expands to $PWD/build/simv

Simv Resolution Order
When VSO.ai resolves the simv executable for a test, it checks sources in this order:
1. simv_location from the build.
2. run_cmd from the build.
3. simv from the build (legacy).
4. Command-line --simv_paths option.
The following example shows a builds section:
simv_location: ${current_dir}/build/simv
comp_vdb_path: ${current_dir}/build/simv.vdb
run_dir: ${current_dir}

- name: bld2
simv_location: ${current_dir}/build2/simv
comp_vdb_path: ${current_dir}/build2/simv.vdb
If comp_vdb_path is specified but the path does not exist, a warning is logged
and the path is not used. This can affect FSM coverage.
