an always statement without a sensitive list, and so on. The following are the
known limitations of the Behavior Analysis engine:
* VHDL Unconstrained Signal
Consider the following example:
entity xxx is port (tttt: out std_logic_vector); end xxx;

The unconstrained signal, tttt, in the example is not supported.
* Verilog Streaming Operator
Consider the following example:
assign

{>>{capi_din}} = a;

The streaming operator {>>{capi_din}}, in the example is not supported.
The BA limitation messages are directed to the haps.log file. The following are some
examples of these log entries:
[BA] Warning:Unconstrained signal(IN1) is not supported.
[BA] Warning:Unconstrained signal(OUT1) is not supported.
[BA] Warning: Streaming operator (assign {>>{capi_din}} = a;
file=case_streamassign.sv,line=5) is not supported.

Navigator Page
The following options are available in the Navigator section:
* Auto Generate Trace With Default Global Type for Selected Signal(s) on Startup:
In Formal navigator flow, automatically generates the waveform when the navigator is
invoked from the selected signals in Source view. It generates the witness waveform
that all signals are non-zero.
* Auto Generate Trace With Default Global Type for Unchecked Property on
Startup: In Formal navigator flow, automatically generates the waveform when the
navigator is invoked from FPV property that has not finished check_fv runs. It tries to
generate CEX waveform (for falsified property), or witness waveform if property does
not have falsified waveform.

Console
The following options are available in the Console section:
* Message Color: The following options are available:
Message Type: It indicates the type of the message: Error, Warning, or Info.
Color: It indicates the color for each message type.
Enable: Turn on this option to enable a particular message type or all message
types.

Use this page to change the general settings associated with the SmartLog window.

Figure 1025 General Page

The following options are available in the General page:
* Specify additional character(s) for word selection: Use this option to specify
additional character(s) for auto selection. Word selection is applied when you doubleclick the text or right-click on the selected text. The selection region is extended when
the text matches the regexp pattern (\w) or the user specified additional character(s).
* Scroll Offset: Use this option to specify the number of context lines you want to see
above the current line.
* PDF Reader Command: Use this option to select the pre-defined PDF Reader
command or enter the preferred PDF Reader command for log files. This setting is
saved in the novas.rc file. The available pre-defined PDF Reader commands are
Figure 1026 PDF Reader Command

* Default Time Unit
Default Display Time Unit: Use this option to specify the default display time unit.
Default Log Time Unit: Use this option to specify the default log time unit.

Default Display Time Unit and Default Log Time Unit preference settings do
not influence the currently opened log files in SmartLog. These settings take
effect when a new SmartLog window is opened and the settings are saved in
the novas.rc file.
* Show simplified message column: Use this option to specify whether the
<Message> column in the structure view shows full message or simplified message.
The simplified message discards the message which is shown in the previous columns,
like, <Severity>, <Time>, and so on.
Off: Shows full message in the <Message> column of structure view.
On: Shows simplified message in the <Message> column of structure view.
* Default Text Wrap Mode: Use this option to specify whether the text appearing in the
SmartLog window is wrapped by default.
Off: Text Wrap mode is disabled by default, that is, the text displayed in the
SmartLog window is not wrapped in accordance with the window width.
On: Text Wrap mode is enabled by default, that is, the text displayed in the
SmartLog window is wrapped to fit the window width.

Rule Page
Use this page to change the rule settings associated with the SmartLog window.
Figure 1027 Rule Page

The following options are available in the Rule page:
* Default Auto Select Rule Mode: Use this option to specify the auto select rule mode.
The following options are available in the Auto Select Rule Mode field:
* Always On: Enables auto-select rule.
* Normal: Enables auto-select rule.
* The Normal mode changes to the Always Off mode, if any partition rule files or
hyperlink rule file is added or removed in the Open Log form and if the Open button is
clicked in the Open Log form.
* Always Off: Disables auto select rule.
* Default Hyperlink Rule: Use this option to specify the hyperlink rule that can be used
as a default rule for SmartLog.

Display Page
Use this page to specify the settings associated with severity.
Figure 1028 Severity Page

You can use this page to specify Display Text and Color for the severity column in the
Structure view of SmartLog window.
To specify Display Text and Color for each severity,
1. Select a severity from the Severity List field.
2. Change the display text in the Display Text field.

3. Change the color in the Color field.
4. Click on Apply or OK to save the settings.

Search Page
Use this page to specify the search settings.
Figure 1029 Search Page

The following options are available in the Search page:
* Enable Loop Searching: Use this option to specify whether the next search starts
over from the first line once the search hits the end of the log.
Off: Loop Searching is disabled, that is, the search stops after it hits the end of the
log.
On: Loop Searching is enabled, that is, the search starts over from the first line after
it hits the end of the log.
* Structure View Search: Hide Blocks Not Matching Search Criteria: Use this option
to specify whether the blocks not matching the search criteria are hidden.
Off: Shows the blocks even if they do not match the search criteria..
On: Hides the blocks not matching the search criteria.

This chapter explains the following utilities:
* verdi, novas, siloti: Commands to invoke the Verdi GUI.
* nWave: A command to invoke the nWave GUI.
* Analysis: A utility to create Certitude setup files.
* Analysis

assertEval: A batch mode command to evaluate assertions.
esa: A command to perform Essential Signal Analysis.
nAnalyzer: A batch mode command for clock analysis and extraction.
nClockTree: A batch mode command for clock tree extraction.
nCompare: A batch mode command to invoke the nCompare module.
* Compilation
aliasextract: A utility that creates an alias file for a precompiled mixed language
bacom: A utility to save the results of Behavior Analysis to the Behavior Database
(BDB).
crdb: A command to perform correlation.
elabcom: A utility that generates the elaboration database.
gencom: A utility that is used to automatically extract the file list (or command list)
from the make file.
libls: A utility to list the contents of the library.
nc2novasrc: A utility to convert the library setting of the NC simulator, cds.lib,
and hdl.var to the novas.rc resource file.
nfixhier: A utility to fix the resolving libraries for the hierarchy of the specified cell.
netlistcom: A utility that performs RTL extraction in the batch mode.
nrun: A batch mode compiler for mixed design files.
spicom: A batch mode compiler for SPICE.
vericom: A batch mode compiler for Verilog (for example, Verilog or SystemVerilog)
designs.
vhdlcom: A batch mode compiler for VHDL.
vlmap: A function that automatically updates library mapping items to the novas.rc
resource file.

* Conversion
esdb2txt: A utility to generate a plain text Essential Signal list from the Essential
Signal Database (ESDB) for emulation flow.
esdbdebug: A utility to dump information in the Essential Signal Database (ESDB)
for debugging.
fsdb2ns: A utility that translates an EPIC FSDB file into an ASCII format and
converts a digital type FSDB file into the Piecewise-Linear (PWL) format.
fsdb2saif: A utility that converts an FSDB file into backward SAIF format.
fsdb2vcd: A utility that translates an FSDB file into VCD.
fsdbdebug: A utility for dumping the FSDB information and generating a log file for
debugging.
fsdbedit: A utility for modifying scope hierarchies in the FSDB file.
fsdbexpand: A utility for processing an existing Essential Signal FSDB file.
fsdbextract: A utility for post processing an existing FSDB file.
fsdbmangle: A utility that mangles signal names in the FSDB file.
fsdbmerge: A utility that merges several FSDB files into a single file.
fsdbrecover: A utility that recovers unfinished FSDB files.
fsdbreport: A utility that reports time sequence, address values, and instruction
values of a simulation.
merge_multi_swp_fsdb: A utility to merge multiple sweep analog FSDB files into a
single FSDB file.
nce2report: A utility to generate a readable waveform comparison report file from
the .nce file.
txt2fsdb: A utility for transferring transactions from a text file to an FSDB file.
txt2uddb: A utility for transferring transactions or messages from a text file to a
UDDB file.
vcd2fsdb: A conversion utility that is used to convert VCD files to FSDB files.
vfast: A conversion utility that is used to convert VCD files to FSDB files.
xloc: A utility to translate signals with X value in an FSDB file into an index file.

* General
novas_plat: A program to obtain the platform information that reflects the platform
used when the Verdi platform is invoked.
* Symbol Libraries
edif2SymDB: A utility that translates EDIF symbol library files into the symbol library.
map2SymDB: A utility that translates a map file into the symbol library.
symDB2map: A utility that translates the symbol library into a map file.
syn2SymDB: A utility that translates library files into a symbol library for the Verdi

General/nTrace Options

-2000

Supports VHDL IEEE 1076-2000 standard.

-2001/+v2k

Supports Verilog IEEE 1364-2001 standard.

-2001genblk

Uses the Verilog IEEE 1364-2001 naming style to
generate blocks (overrides other language options).
IEEE1364-2005 sec12.4.3 unnamed genblk naming is
not applied.
This option only works with -sv or -2005, and
it is for VCS users only (VCS does not support
IEEE1364-2005 sec12.4.3 unnamed genblk naming
through version Y-2006.06-11).

-2005

Supports Verilog IEEE 1364-2005 standard.
IEEE1364-2005 sec12.4.3 unnamed genblk naming is
applied by default.

-2009

Supports SystemVerilog IEEE 1800-2009 standard.

-2012

Supports SystemVerilog IEEE 1800-2012 standard.

-87

Supports VHDL IEEE 1076-1987 standard.

-93

Supports VHDL IEEE 1076-1993 standard.

-aliasIgnoreHier

When specified, apply alias settings to signals with
the same signal name regardless of differences in
the hierarchy. This option is only used with -aliasFile.
For example, verdi -f run.f -aliasFile signal.alias
-aliasIgnoreHier
-------signal.alias-----------FSM_snum 1
FSMsignal system.i_cpu.C1
FSM_anum 2
FSMalias READ 1'b0
FSMalias WRITE 1'b1
FSMname
The alias rule is applied to all signals with the signal
name "C1".

-ams

When this option is specified on the Verdi command
line, HSPICE constructs are recognized. This means
the content between .subckt and .ends are treated as a
comment and a node is added to the design browser to
bind the instance.

-apex
or
-Apex

Opens Verdi in Verdi-APEX mode.

-assert
checker|svaext|
svvunit

Specifies the additional syntax to support. checker:
Supports the checker construct of SystemVerilog IEEE
1800-2009 standard.
svaext: Supports SystemVerilog Assertion features
compliant to IEEE 1800-2009 standard.
svvunit: Supports the PSL vunit syntax. Files with the
*.psl file extension is treated as PSL files.

-autoalias | -aliasFile Specifies -autoalias to automatically extract the
aliasFile
aliases, for example verdi -dbdir simv.daidir
-autoaliasor use -aliasFile to specify an alias file.
The alias file can be automatically created as follows:
1.vericom -f run.f -lib work
2.aliasextract -lib work -output extracted.src_alias
3.verdi -top system -lib work -aliasFile
extracted.src_alias
If multiple alias files need to be loaded, concatenate
them into one alias file and then load it using the
-aliasFile option.

-autoendcelldef

Automatically appends 'endcelldefine at the end of a
file if a matching 'endcelldefine cannot be found for a
declared 'celldefine in the file.

-base
or
-Base

Opens Verdi in Verdi-BASE mode.

-batch

Runs in the batch mode.
The DISPLAY environment variable is not required.
The Verdi platform exits automatically in thirty
seconds if no more Tcl commands are executed in
this mode.

-bdb_load_scope
"pathName"

Specifies the path to load the top module of the
Behavior Database (BDB) file. This option only works
when the -bdb_load option is specified.
> verdi -lib work -top system -bdb_load
work.lib++/work.bdb -bdb_load_scope "system.i_cpu"

-chmod
numeric_mode

Specifies the access attribute for generated files and
directories. For example:verdi 1.v -chmod 777
Changes the log directory (default is vericomLog) and
the library directory (default is work.lib++) to have full
read/write/executable (that is, drwxrwxrwx) access.

-comdir

Specifies the absolute path of the compile
directory.When you load the design with -comdir
<absolute path of the compile dir>, Verdi uses
-comdir directory as the reference directory of the
relative path in KDB to find the location of the source
files. When you load the design without -comdir, Verdi
uses the directory that contains simv.daidir as the
reference directory of the relative paths in KDB, for the
following operations:
* Bring up Source Editor within Verdi to edit the source
files
* OneSearch: search from the source files
* Coverage Source code viewer

-comment_
transoff_regions
-suboption |
+suboption

Skips the source code between translate_off/on
pragmas. The suboptions are vendor names (for
example, cadence, ikos, mentor, novas, pragma,
quickturn, synopsys, synthesis). To skip a single
region, use -suboption. To skip multiple regions, use
+suboption1+suboption2
source code: test.sv
#1
module top;
#2

#3
//mentor translate_off
#4
a = i;
#5
//mentor translate_on
#6
//quickturn translate_off
#7
a = i;
#8
//quickturn translate_on
#9

#10 endmodule

1. Skips a single region verdi
-comment_transoff_regions -mentor test.sv "a=i" on line
#4 is skipped.
2. Skips multiple regions verdi
-comment_transoff_regions+mentor+quickturn
test.sv"a=i"on line #4 and "a=i" on line #7 are skipped.
-cuname
compilation-unit
name

Supports compilation-based compilation-unit mode with
the specified name. The global space is modeled as a
package named compilation-unit name. It is disabled
when the name is specified as -cunit.

-cunit

Supports compilation-based compilation-unit mode with
the default name. The global space is modeled as a
package named novas_cunit_n.

-DEFPARAM
<parameter_path>=
<value>

Changes the specified parameter to the specified value.

-disable_ams_
default_disciplines

Disables the defaults provided by the AMS standard
discipline definition.

+disable_message+
<message_serial_nu
mbers|error|warni
ng>

Suppresses the specified message(s), all error
messages, or all warning messages. Use a plus (+)
symbol for different message type combinations. For
details about each message number and its description,

If used with -vtop, -vtop is ignored.
Configuration File Format
A configuration file may contain four types of
information including Undefined_modules, Virtual_top,
Partial_load, and Exclude.
1.[Undefined_modules]: Suppresses

Example:[Undefined_modules] cpu alu
2.[Virtual_top]: Specifies virtual top mapping

3.[Partial_load]: Specifies tree information to execute
partial load. Example:
If the hierarchy of a design looks like:
- L1c - L2c - L3c - L4c
Top - L1a - L2a - L3a - L4a
- L1b - L2b - L3b - L4b
then, to load the design excluding - L1b - L2b - L3b L4b into the Verdi platform, the partial load section in a
configuration file is edited as follows:

Top.L1a.L2a.L3a.L4a
Top.L1a.L1c
When using partial load, the design is only imported
from the library.
All instantiations under L1c is also loaded.
If both Virtual_top and Partial_load sections are in a
configuration file, the Partial_load section is ignored
and a warning message is displayed.
4. [Exclude]: Specifies excluded modules or scopes.
[Exclude]
CCU
Excludes module instances instantiated by CCU.
[Exclude] system.i_CCU.i_mprom
Exclude system.i_CCU.i_mprom itself and below.

1) When excluding instances, the design is only
imported from the library.

are imported. To keep the consistency of the design

the imported top modules.
The definitions are kept in a .map file
whose syntax is as follows: module_name =
hierarchical_instance_name
The Verdi platform can generate a virtual top
automatically according to the definitions in the .map file
and import only the subset of the design.
Assume a VHDL design whose top module is system
with two instances, cpu and pram, invoked from system.
To load subhierarchies, cpu and pram, into the Verdi
platform instead of loading the whole hierarchy system,
a virtual top file, vtop.map is defined as follows:
cpu = system.i_cpu
pram = system.i_pram
Specifies all the design files obtained in subhierarchy,
cpu and pram, in vtop.f. Then the subset of the design
is imported with the virtual top system by the following

The specified top module must be in a logical
library, (that is, -lib xxx or default library (for
example, work.lib++)); otherwise, it fails. For
example,
verdi -lib libc -L liba -L libb -vtop vtop.map
In the above example, all the modules specified in
vtop.map are found in libc.
The -vtop option is used to specify a virtual top from
the command line without using a .map file:
Specify one virtual top
verdi -f run.f -vtop "CPU=system.i_cpu"
which is equivalent to "verdi -f run.f -vtop vtop.file"
where the content of vtop.file is:
CPU = system.i_cpu
Specify multiple virtual tops
verdi -f run.f -vtop "CPU=system.i_cpu;ALUB =
system.i_ALUB"
which is equivalent to "verdi -f run.f -vtop vtop.file"
where the content of vtop.file is:
CPU = system.i_cpu
ALUB = system.i_ALUB

Verilog/SystemVerilog Syntax and Semantic Parsing
1. If one or more of the following options are specified, parse the syntax/semantic of the
entire design with the newest language type resolved from the -sv, -2001, +v2k, and
-v95 options.
> vericom -v95 +v2k -sv 1.v

The 1.v file is parsed with the SystemVerilog language.
2. If none of the options in the first step are specified, parse the syntax/semantic of the
entire design with Verilog 2001.
Verilog/System Verilog Language Keyword Set Checking
1. If any of the +verilog1995ext, +verilog2001ext, or +systemverilogext options
are specified, check the files specified by +{language}ext against the keyword set of
{language}.
2. If none of the options above are specified and any of the -sv, -2005, -2001, +v2k, or
-v95 options are specified in the command line, check the entire design against the
keyword set of the given language options.
3. If none of the options in 1 and 2 are specified, check the entire design against the
Verilog-2001 keyword set.

Searches for the module definitions of unresolved module instances
in the verdi utility with the following order: 1) Searches the remainder
of the library where the unresolved module instances are found. 2)
Searches through the rest of the libraries. 3) Searches again from the

<libA.v>

<libB.v>

"cellA" is resolved in <libA.v>
> verdi -sv -v libA.v top.v -v libB.v +liborder
"cellA" is resolved in <libB.v>

the Verdi help menu.

1. Evaluate all assertions in the design using default settings and save the assertion
results under the log directory, for example:
./assertEvalLog/evaluate_result.fsdb
> assertEval -sv dut.sv +define+SVA -ssf dut.fsdb

2. Evaluate all assertions in the design with different settings (for example, turn off filtering
for vacuous success and no-match covers and stores all assertion data types) and
generate a text report in the statistics.log file using the following command:
> assertEval -statistic_report statistics.log -store all \
-filter_vacuous_success off -filter_cover_no_match off \ -f run.f -ssf
debug.fsdb

3. Evaluate all assertions of type assume or assert with names matching a_s* in scopes
matching top.m2.checker2.ck* subscopes. Also, generate a text report. For
> assertEval -statistic_report statistics.log \ -prop_list "{-type
assume+assert top.m2.checker2.ck*.a_s*}" \ -lib svlib -top top -ssf
debug.fsdb

4. Multiple arguments of the -prop_list option are supported. For example:
> assertEval -statistic_report statistics.log \ -prop_list "{-type
assume+assert top.m2.checker2.ck*.a_s*} \ {-type assert -level 2
top.m3.assert*} \ {-type cover top.m4.cover*.*check*}" \ -f run.f -ssf
debug.fsdb

5. Evaluate all assertions with assertion type as cover in the top.m1.checker scope and
its next two subscopes.
> assertEval -statistic_report statistics.log \ -prop_file propfile -f
run.f -ssf debug.fsdb

The propfile includes the following line:
-type cover top.m1.checker -level 2

6. Translate Example 4 to use the -prop_file option. For example:
> assertEval -statistic_report statistics.log -prop_file propfile -f
run.f -ssf debug.fsdb

The propfile file includes the following lines:
-type assume+assert top.m2.checker2.ck*.a_s*
-type assert -level 2 top.m3.assert*
-type cover top.m4.cover*.*check*

esa
esa is a batch mode executable for Essential Signal Analysis and is used to generate an

Essential Signal Database (ESDB). The ESDB provides the ability to set the majority of
Essential Signal Analysis (ESA) options at the simulation runtime instead of rerunning
ESA whenever the ESA options need to change. The utility progress is printed to the
screen and the results are saved to the esaLog directory.
Essential Signal Analysis is performed for the specified working scope (using -bas). If
-bas is not specified, esa uses the working scope in the novas.rc resource file (if one
exists); otherwise, the top module of the design (Verilog only) is used.
1. The esa utility requires a Siloti-SimVE license.
2. If the esa utility is used to perform Essential Signal Analysis, the -db option
is added and the output file is an ESDB format file. For example: esa -db
es -top top

3. Set the NOVAS_BATCH_KILL environment variable to 1 when using the esa
utility in LSF environments.

esa [ESA Options] [General Options] [nTrace Options] [Simulator Options]
[Environment Options] [Behavior Analysis Options] [Power Manager
Options]

For details, see General/nTrace Options, Simulator Options, Environment Options,
Behavior Analysis Options, and Power Manager Options sections in the verdi utility
description.

can specify one or more modules. Alternatively,
use -excludefile for specifying multiple modules.
Regular expressions are supported. This option is

1. Generate an ESDB for the full chip:
> esa -f run.f -db es -bas chiptop
es.esdb++ is generated including all Essential Signals in the design.

2. Generate an ESDB for the ALUB module:
> esa -f run.f -db es -bas system.i_CPU.i_ALUB
es.esdb++ is generated including all Essential Signals for the ALUB module.

3. Generate an ESDB for the entire chip excluding the PCU module:
> esa -f run.f -exclude PCU -db es
es.esdb++ is generated including all Essential Signals except those in the PCU

module.

4. List the excluded modules, ranking by percentage the amount the module (for example,
candidates) reduces the Essential Signal count:
> esa -f run.f -db es -bas chiptop -optimalA candidates

where, candidates contains:
#ESA-O: modules suggested to be excluded for saving ES-dump
# size with limited visibility loss
#sequential library cell (~21%)
cell1
#sequential library cell (~12%)
cell2

As the above example shows, cell1 and cell2 are sequential library cells and the ES
count is reduced to 21% and 12% respectively when excluded.

nAnalyzer
The nAnalyzer command is used to invoke batch mode clock analysis and extraction
functions. The command mode helps to reduce memory usage by completing clock
analysis, extracting clocks, and checking crossing paths in the batch mode. The clock
analysis results are saved to a clock database file whose name is "nClock.cdb" by
default. After executing the batch command, invoke the GUI and load the results from
the File -> Load Clock Domain Results command in the nTrace window and the Clock
Domain window gets opened simultaneously. Use the Tools -> List Crossing Paths
command in the Clock Domain window to see the crossing paths, instead of invoking the
Clock Analyzer -> List Crossing Paths command in the nTrace window.
Both "nAnalyzer" and "Verdi" licenses are required and are checked out to execute this

nAnalyzer [Options]

-f filename

Specifies the design file to be imported.

Specifies the library name.

-load filename

Specifies the setting file for clock domain analysis.

-path pathName

Specifies the path of the design file.

-top
topModuleName

Specifies the top module for the imported design.

-translateOn

Ignores the RTL source code between SYNOPSYS
compiler directives synopsys translate_off and synopsys
translate_on.

-vhdl | -verilog

Specifies the language type for importing the design
from the source.

The setting file for -load filename is an rc format file. The syntax for the setting file
is described below along with an example of its use. The setting file uses the pound (#)
sign to designate comment lines and square brackets "[ ]" to define sections. The setting
file includes six sections: [File], [SDC], [CKDomain], [CDC], [Synchronizer], and
[Global]. [TempSection] is also available for each user-defined synchronizer template.
The `@Verdi rc file Version 1.0' line must be the first line in the novas.rc
resource file for the file to be properly recognized by the Verdi platform.
The library settings are loaded from the novas.rc resource file unless the
manage.rc resource file is specified. For details on using the manage.rc file,
see Appendix B: Customizing Verdi.

[File]
This section specifies the name of the clock database. The default value is "nClock.cdb".
ClockDBFile=nClock.cdb

[File]
ClockDBFile=output.cdb

In the above example, the clock database is loaded from output.cdb.

[SDC]
This section defines the Synopsys Design Constraint (SDC) files. You can load multiple
SDC files.
Top = module_name
Item_0 = SDC file1
Item_1 = SDC file2

Item_n = SDC file3

Top = system
Item_0 = TOP.sdc
Item_1 = default.sdc

In the above example, the top module of the SDC is system. The value must be set when
loading SDC files. The SDC files are TOP.sdc and default.sdc.

[CKDomain]
This section specifies the options for Clock Domain Extraction.
Pass = pass module lists
Bypass = bypass module lists
clkSrcOnly = True|False
mergeCell = GATECLK CombLogic
reglist = True|False
separateRegToMultiClkDmn = True|False
traceMultiResolveSource = True|False

In the syntax, the default value of Pass and Bypass is Null. The default value of
clkSrcOnly and traceMultiResolveSource is True. The default value for reglist
and separateRegToMultiClkDmn is False. The default value of mergeCell is GATECLK
CombLogic.

[CDC]
This section specifies the options for Crossing Paths Checking.
CheckBetweenSameDomain = True|False
CheckConvergence = True|False
CheckDivergence = True|False
CheckReconvergence = True|False

In the syntax, the default value of CheckBetweenSameDomain, CheckConvergence,
CheckDivergence, and CheckReconvergence is False.

[Synchronizer]
This section defines the synchronizer settings of Check Crossing Paths. If no
synchronizers are defined, the default value of Item_0 is NULL.
Item_0 = template1
Item_1 = template2

Item_n = templaten

Item_0 = Template sync_1A
Item_1 = Template sync_configuration BBB

In the example, the first synchronizer uses a default template, sync_1, Type_A. The
second synchronizer uses a user-defined configuration, which has a corresponding
[TempSection0].

[Global]
This section specifies the number of templates.
TemplateNum = 0|1

In the syntax, the default value of TemplateNum is 0 if no template is set as the
synchronizer.

[TempSection0]
The example below shows the content of a user-defined synchronizer template. The
content varies depending on the synchronizer type.
Name = BBB
Type = 2
ConnNum = 2
Conn0 = Latch@2
Conn1 = Latch@2

The nCompare utility compares two FSDB files using a defined rule file and reports the
errors to a file.
The nCompare utility supports three kinds of digital data formats: Verilog and VHDL. The
nCompare utility also supports analog and other non-digital data; however, the comparison
is done using the FSDB file format.

The nCompare utility can compare signals of the same value type, and also compare digital
signals with analog signals. The related nce2report utility transforms comparison results
into a readable report, thereby allowing the results to be viewed easily, even in the console
mode.

aliasextract
The aliasextract utility creates an alias file for a precompiled design (Verilog, VHDL, or
mixed). After the alias file is created, it is loaded (using the -aliasFile option) with the
design on the Verdi command line.

aliasextract [Options]

-elab libName

Specifies the elaboration library.
For example, aliasextract -elab
simv.daidir/kdb.elab++

Specifies the library. The default value is work.

-output outputFile

Specifies the output file name. By default, it is saved
to extracted.src_alias in the working directory.

-top moduleName

Specifies the top module.

bacom
The bacom utility saves the results of Behavior Analysis to the Behavior Database (BDB).
The Behavior Database (BDB) is loaded to the Verdi platform by specifying the -bdb_load
option on the novas/verdi command line or through the Behavior Analysis form (invoked
with the Tools -> Temporal Flow View -> Behavior Analysis command in nTrace).

1. The Behavior Database (BDB) must be associated with KDB libraries, so the
design needs to be compiled into libraries (using vericom or vhdlcom) first.
2. The bacom utility forces the BA mode in Working Scope Behavior Analysis
(WSBA).
3. The options in the bacom utility are saved to the bacom.command file in the
bacomLog directory to show how the Behavior Database (BDB) is generated.
You can reuse the BDB.

bacom [Options]

-apimem filename

Specifies a file to define the API memory.

-ba_mode WSBA

Specifies the Behavior Analysis mode. Only
Working Scope Behavior Analysis (WSBA) mode is

-bas "scope(s)" | "*"

Performs Behavior Analysis (with the given scopes
as working scopes) immediately after loading the
design. For example, -bas "{scope1} {scope2}" takes
"scope1" and "scope2" as working scopes and -bas
"{*}" takes all loaded top modules as working scopes.

-bboxEmptyModule 0|1 Specifies whether to define the empty modules as
black boxes.
0: Does not define the empty modules as black

crdb
crdb is a batch mode executable for correlation database (CRDB) extraction. The results
are saved to the crdbLog directory. Correlation extraction is performed for the specified
working scope (using -bas). If -bas is not specified, crdb uses the working scope in the
novas.rc resource file (if one exists); otherwise, the top module of the design (Verilog

only) is used.

1. The crdb utility requires a Siloti-SimVE license.
2. Set the NOVAS_BATCH_KILL environment variable to 1 when using the crdb
utility in LSF environments.

crdb [CRDB Options] [General Options] [nTrace Options] [Simulator
Options] [Environment Options] [Behavior Analysis Options] [Power Manager
Options]

For details, see the General/nTrace Options, Simulator Options, Environment Options,
Behavior Analysis Options, and Power Manager Options sections in the verdi utility. The
following table summarizes the CRDB options:

-G2G "option to load
design"

Within the double quotes behind -G2G, specify the
options needed to load the gate-level design. With
this option, the gate-to-gate mapping is generated.
Use -G2G only with -expMap and the other options
that work with -expMap. Do not use this option with
-RTL/-RTL_FSDB/-GATE. It cannot save CRDB with
the option -crdb.

-GATE "Siloti_options" Within the double quotes behind -GATE, specify the
Siloti options needed to load the gate-level design.
When this option is used with -RTL, the complete
CRDB is generated. Its details are logged to the
<logdir>/GATELog directory. The default value for
<logdir> is crdbLog.
-RTL "Siloti_options"

Within the double quotes behind -RTL, specify
the Siloti options needed to load the RTL design.
When this option is used with -GATE, the complete
CRDB is generated. Its details are logged to the
<logdir>/RTLLog directory. The default value for
<logdir> is crdbLog.

-allreg

When specified, all registers are mapped from the
gate to the RTL for exporting the mapping file. Use this
option with -expMap and do not use this option with
-fsdb or -txt.

-append

Appends data into the CRDB database. This is used in
an incremental build flow for large designs.

-crdb filename

Specifies the working CRDB library name.

-excludeModule

All signals except port signals in excluded modules are
excluded from the mapping file. The port signals in the
excluded modules are listed in the mapping file. Use
this option with the -expMap option.

-expGate

When specified, the correlation analyzer exports gate
objects from the mapping file. This option is optional
and must be used with -expMap.

-expGateUncor

When specified, the correlation analyzer exports
uncorrelated gate objects. This option is optional and
must be used with -expMap.

-expMap filename

Exports the mapping results to the specified file. This
option must be used with only one of the -fsdb, -txt, or
-allreg options.

-expRtl

When specified, the correlation analyzer exports RTL
objects from the mapping file. This option is optional
and must be used with the -expMap option.

-filterModule filename

When specified, all signals in filtered modules are
excluded from the uncorrelated signal list. A new
mapping rate based on the filtered signals is reported.
Use this option with the -expMap option.

-filterInstance filename When specified, all signals in filtered cell instances
are excluded from the uncorrelated signal list. A new
mapping rate based on the filtered signals is reported.
Signal names (ports and nets) are also specified
directly. Use this option with the -expMap option.
-fsdb filename

When specified, all signals in the specified FSDB file
are mapped from the gate to the RTL for exporting the
mapping file. Use this option with the -expMap option
and do not use with -txt or -allreg.

-impMap filename

Specifies the user-defined mapping file. When
specified, the correlation information from the mapping
file is applied to the CRDB and the internal correlation
algorithms are skipped.

-impSVF filename1
Imports the specified files of the synthesis tool
[filename2filenameN] guidance in the SVF format and the register correlation

Specifies a file that contains the list of the synthesis

1. Generate a correlation database for the gate design:
> crdb -GATE "-f run_gate.f -bas top" -crdb extracted.crdb

2. Extract the RTL correlation database and add to the gate extraction, and perform

-target_scope "top.dut" -top_inport

gencom
For ModelSim users, gencom is developed to reduce the effort when importing the
simulator-compiled designs into the Verdi platform. gencom uses the existing environment
setup, modelsim.ini, for ModelSim. It generates a command list or file list that contains
all of the compiled source files in the ModelSim libraries and keeps the correct library
dependency and compile dependency. Use the generated command list or file list to import
the VHDL/Verilog designs into the Verdi platform.
gencom supports several vlog language options (for example, -2001, -sv, and
-vlog95compat) as described below:

1. vlog uses the 2001 standard as the default language and vericom uses
95; therefore, gencom automatically generates commands for vericom
with -2001 as the default. For example, when vlog a.v is used, gencom
generates the following:
vericom -2001 +systemverilogext+.sv a.v.

2. vlog enables the SystemVerilog support if either of the following exists:
a. With the -sv option
b. The file has an -sv file extension
In (a), if vlog is used with -sv, gencom generates commands for vericom
with -sv. For example, when vlog -sv a.v is used, gencom generates
'vericom -2001 -sv a.v' (+systemverilog+.sv is redundant).
In (b), vericom has an option similar to +systemverilogext+.sv to
support SystemVerilog parsing for .sv files. gencom automatically generates
commands for vericom with +systemverilogext+.sv as the default. For
example, when 'vlog a.sv' is used, gencom generates 'vericom -2001
+systemverilogext+.sv a.sv'.
3. vlog has the -vlog95compat option to disable the 2001 standard and
SystemVerilog support (both situations, 2(a) and 2(b) are overridden). If
vlog is used with this option and -sv, gencom generates commands for
vericom without the -2001, -sv, and +systemverilogext+.sv options.
For example, when 'vlog -vlog95compat -sv a.sv' is used, gencom
generates 'vericom a.sv'.

gencom [Options]

Generates output as a file list. By default, gencom generates a
command list. To see the format for the file list and command
list, refer the NOTE below.

Outputs the full path for each design file name.

Shows the usage for the Leapfrog environment.

generated from MTI.

Specifies a dedicated VHDL library to extract. gencom
extracts the source files that are compiled in this specified
ModelSim library.

-map mapFile Uses a map file to specify the source file searching paths for
libraries. For the format of map_file, see the NOTE below.
-nrc

Do not auto update the novas.rc resource file. The default is
auto update the library mapping in the novas.rc resource file.

-o file

Specifies the output file name. Its default value is run.com.

-skipothers

Skips the other references in the modelsim.ini file.

-tf filename

Specifies a dedicated VHDL design file to extract. Without
this option, gencom extracts all of the source files for those
libraries specified in the modelsim.ini file.

1. The format of map_file is as follows:
Modelsim_initial_file = <full_path/modelsim_initial_file>
<library_name = "search_path";;"search_path">
<library_name = "search_path";;"search_path">
.
.
OTHERS=<"search_path";; "search_path">

For example, gencom.map is the map file and contains the following:
modelsim_initial_file = "./modelsim.ini"
work = ".";"../src_dir"
vital = "."
memory = "../src_dir"
OTHERS = "."

If the paths of the source files are updated after using vcom to compile
ModelSim's libraries or the source files are not specified with their full path
to use vcom to compile source files into ModelSim libraries, gencom is unable
to find those source files from the specified ModelSim's initial file in the map
file. With the <library_name= Paths of the source files> in the map
file, gencom can extract the exhausted source files of the design.
2. The format of the command list is as follows:
vhdlcom -work libraryName <path>/source_file (for VHDL
source code)
vericom -work libraryName <path>/source_file (for Verilog
source code)

The example of the command list file is as follows:
run.com

work ../src/packageCPU.vhd
work ../src/maprom.vhd
work ../src/microrom.vhd
work ../src/pram.vhd
alub_lib ./arithlogic.vhd
alub_lib ./ALU.vhd
ccu_lib ./CCU.vhd
pcu_lib ./PCU.vhd
cpu_lib ./CPU.vhd
work ../testbench/system.vhd

The format of the file list is as follows:
<path/source_file>

The example of the file list is as follows:

../src/packageCPU.vhd
../src/maprom.vhd
../src/microrom.vhd
../src/pram.vhd

Use the -filelist option to generate a file list that is imported easily
into the Verdi platform. gencom generates a command list output if the
design includes different VHDL options, even if the -filelist option is

already applied. This includes source files that use VHDL-87 and some
use VHDL-93, mixed-language designs, or designs that are compiled into
multiple libraries to run the simulation. Under these circumstances, you
cannot use a file list to compile and import the design into the Verdi platform.

nc2novasrc is a utility that converts the library setting of the NC simulator, cds.lib and
hdl.var, to the novas.rc resource file. The library mappings from cds.lib, including
the nested cds.lib files, are extracted and the corresponding [Library] section is built
into the novas.rc resource file. Some predefined libraries, such as ieee, std, synopsys,
vital2000, and novas, are skipped. LIB_MAP and VIEW_MAP from hdl.var, including
nested hdl.var files, are also extracted and the corresponding [NC_Sim] section built into
the novas.rc resource file.

vericom
vericom is a batch mode compiler for Verilog languages (for example, Verilog,
Verilog-2001, and SystemVerilog). vericom checks and saves the Verilog design into a
library. By default, vericom updates existing modules in the library.

1. The default Verilog compile mode is Verilog-2001.
2. Loading gzipped (*.gz) files for the Verilog design is supported.

3. The library settings are loaded from the novas.rc resource file unless the
manage.rc resource file is specified. For details on using the manage.rc
resource file, see Appendix B: Customizing Verdi.
4. The -ssy, -ssz, and -ssv options must not be used if the compiled gatelevel design is used with the nECO module for ECO modification.

Verilog-2001 Configuration
Configuration is a Verilog-2001 construct. Configuration constructs consist of two parts:
library mapping and configurations. The library mapping is used at compilation to
determine which library to compile the source. The configuration is a set of rules to apply
when searching for a design unit to bind to an instance.
The Verdi platform treats library mapping and configuration as two independent constructs.
Library mapping is not part of a Verilog design. It is treated as a library setting for vericom
only. A configuration is treated as part of the Verilog design, like VHDL configurations.
Library Map
Library mapping is only effective when using the vericom utility to compile the design. The
library map file is specified using the -libmap command-line option.
-libmap <filename>: Specifies the library mapping file.
vericom is used to compile the design into the libraries specified in the library maps. You

must explicitly specify the library map file. For example:
[test.map]
library rtlLib *.v
library gateLib *.vg
include lib2.map
> vericom -libmap test.map *.v *.vg

Configuration
A configuration is treated as a new kind of Verilog design unit. If the Verilog configuration
is used, the configuration must be compiled into the library and the design imported by
explicitly specifying the configuration as the top module. For example:
[gate.cfg]
config mux_cfg_gate;
design work.mux_tb;
default liblist rtllib
instance mux_tb.dut.i1 liblist gatelib
endconfig
> vericom -2001 gate.cfg
> verdi -top mux_cfg_gate

1. Library mapping and configurations can exist in the same or different files.
2. Multiple library map files are used but each file must be preceded by the
-libmap option.
3. The library declaration cannot be overridden. For example, only the first
library declaration is effective (same as ModelSim):
library rtllib ./mux81.v;
library rtllib ./mux41_rtl.v;
library rtllib ./mux21.v;

4. Module resolution priority:
a. Instance-clause has higher priority than cell-clause.
b. The -Lf option has higher priority than default liblist (following the
convention of ModelSim).
c. The default liblist has higher priority than NC uselib lib=,
(following the convention of NC).
Limitation:
1. Library mappings are only used in the vericom utility.
2. Configurations must be compiled into a library and be loaded (used) from a
library. You cannot use a configuration when importing the design into the
Verdi platform from the source files directly.
3. Configurations cannot be applied to instance arrays and generated
instances.
4. Elaboration for the following coding style is not supported:
cell libA.cpu use top.myCPU

fsdb2ns is a utility to translate an EPIC FSDB file into the ASCII format and convert a
digital type FSDB file into the Piecewise Linear (PWL) format. The output format (-fmt) is

PWL depending on the specified format.

In the PWL format, some or all signals with delays are extracted to a new ASCII file. Note
that only two types of the signals are handled:
v - Analog voltage (PWL, voltage resolution)
i - Instantaneous current (Piecewise Constant (PWC), current resolution)

Other signals, even though they are specified with -s, are ignored. The value changes of
instantaneous current signals, which are PWC signals, are converted to the PWL format
by only keeping the first value change in the same time step.
fsdb2ns only keeps the upper-most signal of all equivalent signals when converting all

signals (not a signal list), and converts all signals when a signal list is specified.

To specify the top scopes for Spice created analog FSDB files:
1. If the original FSDB file has scopes, it creates scopes specified by scope_name above
the original scopes.
Consider the original hierarchy as follows and scope_name as s1.s2:
begin tree
scope A;
var va;
upscope;
end tree

It creates two scopes before scope A and the generated FSDB hierarchy is as follows:
begin tree
Scope s1
Scope s2
Scope A
var va;
end tree

2. If the signal name is in format I(xxx), or V(xxx), or other start code followed with the
opening parenthesis '(' character and the closing parenthesis ')' character, scope_name
is put in after the closing parenthesis '(' character. For example, if the original signal
name is I(a.b), scope_name is x.y, the generated FSDB has a signal named as
I(x.y.a.b).

3. If the original scope does not exist, it adds scope_name before the original signal name.
For example, if the original signal name is a.b, scope_name is x.y, the generated
FSDB has a signal named as x.y.a.b.
4. If the original signal name starts with the backslash (\) character, it adds scope_name
before the original signal name though the addition is after the first backslash (\)
character. For example, if the original signal name is \\a.b, the generated FSDB file
has a signal named as \\x.y.a.b.
5. For mixed EPIC FSDB files, the -add_top_analog_scope option only applies to
analog signals. Digital signals remain unchanged.
The original hierarchy is as follows:
begin tree
Scope A
var: digital_var
Scope B
var: I(analog_var)
end tree

After executing this following command:
fsdbedit source.fsdb -add_top_analog_scope "aa" -o dest.fsdb

The dest.fsdb hierarchy becomes as follows:
begin tree
Scope A
var: digital_var
Scope B
var: I(aa.analog_var)
end tree

fsdbexpand
fsdbexpand is a utility to process an existing Essential Signal FSDB file. With this utility,

you can expand signals, scopes, and time periods of interest to a new FSDB file without
rerunning time-consuming simulations. The fsdbexpand utility requires the design (using

-f or -lib) and the Essential Signal FSDB file to be specified; the signal/scope list and

time range options are optional.

The options are passed to the Siloti system in a non-GUI mode where Behavior Analysis
and Data Expansion are performed and the new FSDB file is saved. The new FSDB file is
used with other utilities (for example, fsdbreport, fsdb2vcd) or sent to another engineer
for further analysis.
1. The fsdbexpand utility requires a Siloti-SimVE license.
2. For reasonable performance and memory consumption, the
recommendation is to use fsdbexpand for a limited number of (<100k)
signals and (<100k) cycles at a time.
3. If the SKIP_CELL_INSTANCE environment variable is set to 1, library cells are
skipped (not expanded) by the fsdbexpand utility.
4. Set the NOVAS_BATCH_KILL environment variable to 1 when using the
fsdbexpand utility in LSF environments.

[Simulator Options] [Environment Options] [Behavior Analysis Options]
[Power Manager Options]

fsdbextract
fsdbextract is a utility to post-process an existing FSDB file. This utility extracts signals,

scopes, and time periods of interest to a new FSDB file without rerunning time-consuming
simulations. Depending on the dumped signal, the full or partial range of a bus signal are
extracted. Also, the FSDB file can be split into multiple files by size constraint.
1. fsdbextract supports extracting FSDB files with transaction-type
signals and local variables. If the FSDB file contains glitches and the
FSDB_ENV_MAX_GLITCH_NUM environment variable is:
a. Set to 0, all glitches are extracted.
b. Set to 1 or not set (the default value), no glitches are extracted to the
new FSDB files.
c. Set to 2, the first and the last values of glitches are extracted. For
At time 100ns, if the values are 0, 1, x, z, then 0 and z are recorded.
At time 100ns, if the values are 0, 1, x, 0, then only 0 is recorded.
d. Set to 3, the first two and the last values are extracted. If the value
of the FSDB_ENV_MAX_GLITCH_NUM environment variable is changed,
fsdbextract needs to be rerun for the new value to take effect.
2. For the -s or -f options, if the specified signals are not found in the FSDB
file, the setting of this environment variable impacts the results as follows:
a. If the NOVAS_FSDBEXTRACT_DISABLE_EXIT_ON_ERROR environment
variable is set (null, 0, 1, included), warning messages stating that the
specified signals do not exist in the <rtl.fsdb> FSDB file are displayed

(for example, *WARN* Command line: signal </a/b> does not
exist in the input file <rtl.fsdb>.) and an FSDB file containing
only the found signals are generated.
b. If the NOVAS_FSDBEXTRACT_DISABLE_EXIT_ON_ERROR environment
variable is not set, error messages stating that the specified signals
do not exist in the <rtl.fsdb> FSDB file are displayed (for example,

*ERROR* Command line: signal </a/b> does not exist in the
input file <rtl.fsdb>.) and the program exits.

3. If the FSDB file includes transaction data, the transaction data is ignored
and only RTL signals in the FSDB file are extracted.

fsdbextract fsdb_file_name [Options]

Specifies the start time of the extraction. If omitted, the start
time of the FSDB is used. The time unit is Ms|Ks|s|ms|us|ns|
ps|fs. The default time unit is ns.

-compact

Creates value changes in a compact format. This option may
reduce file size but takes longer to create the FSDB file.

Specifies the end time of the extraction. If omitted, the end
time of the FSDB is used. The time unit is Ms|Ks|s|ms|us|ns|

override those in config_file. The Tcl commands are as

Splits the extracted FSDB file into multiple files with the size

The split files are named with a 5-bit serial number before
.fsdb (for example, XXX00001.fsdb, XXX00002.fsdb,
XXX0000n.fsdb).

and signals/scopes containing them are double quoted

example, "*/data" matches /top_module/data but cannot

-seq

Turns on sequence number dumping for the extracted
FSDB file when the source file contains sequence number
information. Sequence number dumping records the order
of value changes that occur on different signals at the same

-time_shift
time[unit]

Specifies the time offset for the extraction. If omitted, no time
shift is applied. The time unit is optional and is Ms|Ks|s|ms|
us|ns|ps|fs. The default time unit is ns. The time is positive
or negative. For example, assuming the original FSDB has a
time range of 10-100ns, when time shift is 20ns, the extracted
FSDB file has a time range from 30ns to 120ns. When time
shift is -5ns, the extracted FSDB file has a time range from
5ns to 95ns.

-tscale
time[unit]

Specifies the time scale unit for the extracted FSDB file. The
specified time must be positive. The time unit is Ms|Ks|s|ms|
us|ns|ps|fs. The default time unit is ns.
The fsdbextract -tscale option only modifies the scale unit
of fsdb file. It does not modify the value or change time for
each signal.

text:
Specifies a configuration file for the imported design.
Partial load and excluded instances is only used with
import from library; undefined modules and virtual top
are used with both import from library and import from
If used with -vtop, -vtop is ignored.
Configuration File Format
A configuration file may contain four types of
information including Undefined_modules, Virtual_top,
Partial_load, and Exclude.
1.[Undefined_modules]: Suppresses
warning messages of undefined modules.
Example:[Undefined_modules] cpu alu
2.[Virtual_top]: Specifies virtual top mapping
information. Example:
[Virtual_top] system = vaTop.sys CPU = vbTop.t_cpu
3.[Partial_load]: Specifies tree information to execute
partial load. Example:
If the hierarchy of a design looks like:
- L1c - L2c - L3c - L4c
Top - L1a - L2a - L3a - L4a
- L1b - L2b - L3b - L4b
then, to load the design excluding - L1b - L2b - L3b L4b into the Verdi platform, the partial load section in a
configuration file is edited as follows:
[Partial_load]
Top.L1a.L2a.L3a.L4a
Top.L1a.L1c
When using partial load, the design is only imported
from the library.
All instantiations under L1c is also loaded.
If both Virtual_top and Partial_load sections are in a
configuration file, the Partial_load section is ignored
and a warning message is displayed.
4. [Exclude]: Specifies excluded modules or scopes.
[Exclude]
CCU
Excludes module instances instantiated by CCU.
[Exclude] system.i_CCU.i_mprom
Exclude system.i_CCU.i_mprom itself and below.

This option is used with the -top and -lib option. For

Starts searching from the parent library first. The

-liblist option.
<top.sv>
module top;

> vericom -lib top -sv top.sv
The top.sv file is compiled as top.lib++.
> vericom -lib L1 -sv M.sv
The M.sv file is compiled as L1.lib++.
> Verdi -top top -lib top -liblist L1
Searching top.m finds module M in L1.lib++.
> Verdi -top top -lib top -liblist L1 -liblist_work
Searching top.m finds module M in top.lib++. The -liblist
option is ignored.

queue when a license is not immediately available.
This option ensures that Verdi pauses and waits for a
license to be released rather than failing due to license
unavailability.
Note that the VERDI_FEAT_PKG_MODE_UPWARD
environment variable is not supported when using
license queuing with the -licqueue option.

dumpFile(s)| fastFile (*.fsdb.gz), bzip2 FSDB (*.fsdb.bz2), waveform dump

(*.vcd, *.vcd.gz) files, or FSDB file lists (*.flst).
For individual FSDB files, 1 - 16 files may be specified

or

For a file list, each FSDB or virtual file must be listed on

Unlimited files are supported. A pound (#) sign and a
semicolon (;) character are used for comments, but they
must be on separate lines. For example:### Normal
FSDB file with full path

../mod2/file3.fsdb

+systemverilogext+

Use it in place of the -sv option.

text:
Specifies the top modules for the imported design.
Verilog modules are case-sensitive. The top
module name can be specified using the Cadence
NC simulator command format to elaborate
the designated design unit, such as ncelab
[library.]cell[:view]
Example: verdi -nclib -top "novas.top(rtl)"
The Verdi platform elaborates top in the library novas
and view rtl. When the library is not specified, search
work.lib++ for the top design unit.
Example: verdi -nclib -top top is same as verdi -nclib
-lib work -top top or verdi -nclib -top work.top
Multiple top modules in the same library are supported.
Example: verdi -top "top1 top2 top3"
When multiple top modules from different libraries are
required, use the following format:
verdi -top "libA.top1 libB.top2 libC.top3"
The Verdi platform invokes three hierarchy trees for
top1, top2, and top3.

-translateOn

Ignores the RTL source code between SYNOPSYS
compiler directives "synopsys translate_off" and
"synopsys translate_on."

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Specifies a virtual top file for import designs. Instead of
importing the entire design, some subsets of the design
are imported. To keep the consistency of the design
hierarchy between simulation results and imported
design files, specify the correct hierarchical names of
the imported top modules.
The definitions are kept in a .map file
whose syntax is as follows: module_name =
hierarchical_instance_name
The Verdi platform can generate a virtual top
automatically according to the definitions in the .map file
and import only the subset of the design.
Assume a VHDL design whose top module is system
with two instances, cpu and pram, invoked from system.
To load subhierarchies, cpu and pram, into the Verdi
platform instead of loading the whole hierarchy system,
a virtual top file, vtop.map is defined as follows:
cpu = system.i_cpu
pram = system.i_pram
Specifies all the design files obtained in subhierarchy,
cpu and pram, in vtop.f. Then the subset of the design
is imported with the virtual top system by the following
verdi -vtop vtop.map -vhdl -f vtop.f

The specified top module must be in a logical
library, (that is, -lib xxx or default library (for
example, work.lib++)); otherwise, it fails. For
example,
verdi -lib libc -L liba -L libb -vtop vtop.map
In the above example, all the modules specified in
vtop.map are found in libc.
The -vtop option is used to specify a virtual top from
the command line without using a .map file:
Specify one virtual top
verdi -f run.f -vtop "CPU=system.i_cpu"
which is equivalent to "verdi -f run.f -vtop vtop.file"
where the content of vtop.file is:
CPU = system.i_cpu
Specify multiple virtual tops
verdi -f run.f -vtop "CPU=system.i_cpu;ALUB =
system.i_ALUB"
which is equivalent to "verdi -f run.f -vtop vtop.file"
where the content of vtop.file is:
CPU = system.i_cpu
ALUB = system.i_ALUB

1.vhd

Use -vtopvhdl with -vtop.
-wcFile

Supports the wildcard file list in a run.f file. Specify this
option before -f. Note that the /**/ comment syntax is
not supported in the run.f file.

-workMode

user_defined_mode]

Specifies the work mode or the user-defined mode. This
option is ignored if the -ssr option is also specified. For
details on the different work modes and instructions
for saving a user mode, see the Window Commands
section of the nTrace chapter.

-wreal
resolution_function

Supports only the "wreal" keyword in Verilog-AMS.
This option also supports the "wrealXState" or

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Specifies the Verilog-XL simulation executable and
enables the interactive mode.

-xprop=
tmerge|xmerge|
config_file

Specifies the X-propagation format. Its default value is
tmerge.
tmerge: Use the tmerge mode.
xmerge: Use the xmerge mode.
config_file: Use the user-defined setup file that contains
the X-propagation configurations.
verdi -f run.f -ssf myfile.fsdb -xprop=xmerge -xproplog
"xprop.log"

This option can be used with the -i option.

It is recommended to specify the same mode
(tmerge or xmerge) as specified when running VCS.
If the tmerge and xmerge arguments get specified
multiple times for -xprop (in any order), only the last
specification is recognized and takes effect. If the
configuration file argument gets specified with any
other argument, an error is issued.

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Specifies the X-propagation log file. Multiple log files
are supported by enclosing files with double quotes.
Loading the xprop.log.gz file with this option is also
supported, but only a single file is allowed for this
compressed file.
This option is only valid after the -xprop option is
Example: verdi -f run.f -ssf myfile.fsdb -xprop=xmerge
-xproplog "xprop1.log xprop2.log"

Verilog/SystemVerilog Syntax and Semantic Parsing
1. If one or more of the following options are specified, parse the syntax/semantic of the
entire design with the newest language type resolved from the -sv, -2001, +v2k, and
-v95 options.
> vericom -v95 +v2k -sv 1.v

The 1.v file is parsed with the SystemVerilog language.
2. If none of the options in the first step are specified, parse the syntax/semantic of the
entire design with Verilog 2001.
Verilog/System Verilog Language Keyword Set Checking
1. If any of the +verilog1995ext, +verilog2001ext, or +systemverilogext options
are specified, check the files specified by +{language}ext against the keyword set of
{language}.
2. If none of the options above are specified and any of the -sv, -2005, -2001, +v2k, or
-v95 options are specified in the command line, check the entire design against the
keyword set of the given language options.
3. If none of the options in 1 and 2 are specified, check the entire design against the
Verilog-2001 keyword set.
Environment Options

-envinfo

Dumps environment variable descriptions.

-envmap

Shows the mapping for all environment variables.

-envset

the command line. Use a plus (+) symbol as the
delimiter. The option can be specified multiple times.
-envset ENV1=A+ENV2=B
-envset "ENV3=1 2 3+ENV4=C"

title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
-rcinfo

Dumps key descriptions of the resource file.

-sdfDelay [Min|Typ|Max] Specifies the delay type for use with SDF annotation.
Its options are:
Min: Minimum Delay
Typ: Typical Delay
Max: Maximum Delay

The following environment options are also supported:
Simulator Options
All simulator options are accepted by the Verdi platform. The options it needs to compile
the design are used and the rest are ignored. For a complete list and details, refer to the
documentation for the simulator. The following simulator command line options are also
commonly used by the Verdi platform:

+define+<macro>

The +define option is used to specify macros. If the macro is also
defined in the source code, it is overridden by this option.

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Invokes Verdi with an attached simulation mode. <sim_pid>: The
simulation process ID which you want to attach.

+incdir+<directoryna
me>

Specifies the search path for files used by the include statement.

+libext+<extensionna
me>

Specifies the file extensions for Verilog library files. See also the -y

+liborder

Searches for the module definitions of unresolved module instances
in the verdi utility with the following order: 1) Searches the remainder
of the library where the unresolved module instances are found. 2)
Searches through the rest of the libraries. 3) Searches again from the
first library.
<top.v>
module top;
cellA ca();
<libA.v>
module cellA;
<libB.v>
module cellA;
> verdi -sv -v libA.v top.v -v libB.v +librescan
"cellA" is resolved in <libA.v>
> verdi -sv -v libA.v top.v -v libB.v +liborder
"cellA" is resolved in <libB.v>

+librescan

Searches for the module definitions of unresolved module instances
by always starting from the first library in the library list specified on
the Verdi command line. For examples, see the +liborder option in the
verdi utility description.

+libverbose

Prints a message in the verdiLog/compiler.log file to indicate the library
file where the instance is resolved when a module is instantiated in the
source file or library files.
This option does not take effect when importing the design from the
library.

text:
Loads the OVM library for compilation. The +define+VCS option is
added automatically on the Verdi command line.
To compile the external OVM library, first set the VCS_HOME or
VCS_OVM_HOME environment variable. The VCS_OVM_HOME
environment variable has higher priority than VCS_HOME. If both
VCS_OVM_HOME and VCS_HOME are set, and ovm.sv cannot
be found in $VCS_OVM_HOME, an error is reported.
setenv
VCS_HOME /simulator/Synopsys/VCS_vH-2013.06/vcs_vH-2013.06>
verdi -sv -ntb_opts ovm test.v
Example 2: > setenv
VCS_HOME /simulator/Synopsys/VCS_vH-2013.06/vcs_vH-2013.06
> verdi -sv +define+VCS+incdir+$VCS_HOME/etc/ovm/src
\$VCS_HOME/etc/ovm/src/ovm_pkg.sv
\+incdir+$VCS_HOME/etc/ovm/src/vcs
\$VCS_HOME/etc/ovm/src/vcs/ovm_custom_install_vcs_recorder.sv
test.v

title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Loads the VMM library for compilation. The
+define+VCS+VMM_IN_PACKAGE option is added automatically on
the Verdi command line.
To compile the external VMM library, first set the VCS_HOME
environment variable.
setenv
VCS_HOME /
tools/simulator/Synopsys/VCS_vH-2013.06/vcs_vH-2013.06> verdi -sv
-ntb_opts vmm test.v
> setenv VCS_HOME /tools/simulator/Synopsys/> verdi -sv
+define+VCS+VMM_IN_PACKAGE \+incdir+$VCS_HOME/etc/rvm
\$VCS_HOME/etc/rvm/vmm.sv test.v
For the usage of mixed UVM and RVM libraries, see the Mixed Usage
of UVM and RVM Libraries columns.

-ntb_opts
uvm[-<version>]

Loads the UVM library for compilation. The +define+VCS option is
added automatically on the Verdi command line.
To compile the external UVM library, first set the VCS_HOME or
VCS_UVM_HOME environment variable. The VCS_UVM_HOME
environment variable has higher priority than VCS_HOME. If both
VCS_UVM_HOME and VCS_HOME are set, and uvm_pkg.sv
cannot be found in $VCS_UVM_HOME, an error is reported.
setenv
VCS_UVM_HOME /
$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm<version>/lib/src> verdi -sv
-ntb_opts uvm test.v
> setenv
VCS_UVM_HOME /
$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm<version>/lib/src
> verdi -sv +define+VCS +incdir+$VCS_UVM_HOME
\$VCS_UVM_HOME/uvm.sv \+incdir+$VCS_UVM_HOME/vcs \
$VCS_UVM_HOME/vcs/uvm_custom_install_vcs_recorder.sv
\+incdir+$VCS_UVM_HOME/verdi
\$VCS_UVM_HOME/verdi/uvm_custom_install_verdi_recorder.sv
test.v
If the VCS_UVM_HOME environment variable is not set, the UVM
library path in the VCS_HOME environment variable is used. The
following paths and files are added automatically:
+incdir+$VCS_HOME/etc/uvm[-<version>] \
$VCS_HOME/etc/uvm[-<version>]/uvm.sv \
$VCS_HOME/etc/uvm[-<version>]/vcs \
$VCS_HOME/etc/uvm[-<version>]/vcs/uvm_custom_install_vcs_record
er.sv \
+incdir+$VCS_HOME/etc/uvm[-<version>/verdi
\$VCS_HOME/etc/uvm[-<version>/verdi/uvm_custom_install_verdi_rec
order.sv
For the usage of mixed UVM and RVM libraries, see the Mixed Usage
of UVM and RVM Libraries columns.

Mixed Usage of UVM
and RVM Libraries
:-ntb_opts
uvm[-$version]+rvm,-ntb
_opts
rvm+uvm[-$version],ntb_opts uvm[-$version]
-ntb_opts rvm

title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
When using mixed UVM and RVM libraries, the options in the leading
column are equivalent to the following:
+define+VCS \
+define+VCS+VMM_IN_PACKAGE \
+incdir+<vmm_lib_path>/etc/rvm \
<vmm_lib_path>/etc/rvm/vmm.sv \
<uvm_lib_path>/src/uvm_vmm_pkg.sv \
+incdir+<uvm_lib_path>/src \
<uvm_lib_path>/src/uvm.sv \
+incdir+<uvm_lib_path>/src/vcs \
<uvm_lib_path>/vcs/uvm_customer_install_vcs_recorder.sv \
+define+VMM_UVM_INTEROP
To turn off the automatic inclusion of uvm_vmm_pkg.sv, use
+define+NO_VMM_UVM_INTEROP in the two-step flow
(that is, compile and import design from libraries) and use
+define+NO_UVM_VMM_INTEROP in the UUM flow.
<uvm_lib_path> is determined by $VCS_UVM_HOME or
$VCS_HOME. <vmm_lib_path> is determined by $VCS_HOME.
Specify the UVM_ON_TOP and VMM_ON_TOP options when
using mixed UVM and RVM libraries.

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
-ovm
[-<version>]

Load the default Verdi OVM library. If -ovm and -ovmhome are
specified at the same time, -ovm is ignored.-<version> is used to
specify a non default library. All available library versions are located
in the $VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/ovm directory. For example, the
available ovm version is: ovm-2.1.2
When only -ovm is specified, the default is ovm-2.1.2. The
+define+INCA option is added automatically on the Verdi command
line.
> verdi -ovm test.v
> verdi -sv +define+INCA \
+incdir+$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/ovm/ovm-2.1.2/lib/src
\$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/ovm/ovm-2.1.2/lib/src/ovm_pkg.sv test.v

-ovmhome
<path>

Specifies the OVM installation directory. The +define+INCA option is
added automatically on the Verdi command line.
> verdi -sv -ovmhome $MyOVM test.v
> verdi -sv +define+INCA +incdir+$MyOVM/src \
$MyOVM/src/ovm_pkg.sv test.v

Specifies the path of the simulation binary file. The path must be
double quoted. This option can be used without the -simType option. If
-simType is not specified, the default setting in the novas.rc resource
file is used.
verdi -sv f.sv -simBin "/rcc2/integ/SOL2/deb6.1/nvfy/bin/start.simv"

-simOpt 'option1
option2 optionN'

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Specifies simulation options. A pair of single quotes (') must be used to
enclose the options. Example: verdi -sv f.sv -simOpt '+vcs+lic+wait+"
TEST\" '

-simType
<VCS|ModelSim|NC>

Specifies the simulator (VCS, ModelSim or NC) to use. The simulator
is not case-sensitive.

-uvm
[-<version>]

Loads the default Verdi UVM library. If -uvm and -uvmhome are
specified at the same time, -uvm is ignored. -<version> is used to
specify a non-default library. All available library versions are located
in the $VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm directory. For example, the
available uvm versions are:
uvm-1.0p1 uvm-1.1d

When only -uvm is specified, the default is uvm-1.1d. The
+define+INCA option is added automatically on the Verdi command
line.
In the following examples, Example 1 is equivalent to Example
2.Example 1:
> verdi -uvm test.v
> verdi -sv +define+INCA \
+incdir+$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm-1.1d/lib/src \
$VERDI_HOME/share/vmlib/uvm/uvm-1.1d/lib/src/uvm.sv test.v

-uvmDebug

When this option is specified and VCS is specified as the simulator
type, the following VCS runtime options is automatically appended in
the Interactive Simulation Debug mode when the Verdi platform starts
the simv binary:
+UVM_CONFIG_DB_TRACE
+UVM_PHASE_TRACE
+UVM_RESOURCE_DB_TRACE
+UVM_OBJECTION_TRACE
+UVM_FACTORY_TRACE
+UVM_LOG_RECORD
+UVM_VERDI_TRACE=UVM_AWARE,
For details about the VCS runtime options, see the UVM Debug: option
in the Simulation page of the Preferences form.

-uvmhome
<path>

Specifies the UVM installation directory. The +define+INCA option is
added automatically on the Verdi command line.
> verdi -sv -uvmhome $MyUVM test.v
> verdi -sv +define+INCA +incdir+$MyUVM/src \
$MyUVM/src/uvm.sv test.v

chapter: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value
text:
Modules in the specified file are treated as library cells. This option is
overwritten if the -ssv option is specified.

-v_no_elab

Library modules in all library files (-v) are elaborated. This option is
overwritten if the -ssv option is specified.

-y
<directoryname>

Modules in the specified directory are treated as library cells. This
option is overwritten if the -ssy option is specified. In the directory, the
library file name is supposed to be the same as the module name.
The +libext option is also used to check the library file extension and
ensure that the library file is matched.
Assume the following file hierarchy for the current directory:
top.v ydir/cpu.v ydir/alu.sv
The file names and module names are as follows:<top.v> module
top; cpu c1(); alu a1(); endmodule <cpu.v> module cpu; endmodule
<alu.sv> module alu; endmodule
When the following commands are executed on the current directory,
the following are the results:
> verdi -sv top.v -y ydir
When +libext+.v+.sv is not specified, the following two messages are
issued:
*Error* view cpu is not defined for instance c1 "top.v", 2:
*Error* view alu is not defined for instance a1 "top.v", 3:
> verdi -sv top.v -y ydir +libext+.v
*Error* view alu is not defined for instance a1 "top.v", 3:
> verdi -sv top.v -y ydir +libext+.v+.sv
Error and warning are not issued.

-y_no_elab

Library modules in all library directories (-y) are not elaborated. This
option is overwritten if the -ssy option is specified.

-z_no_elab

Cell modules (celldefine) are not elaborated. This option is overwritten
if the -ssz option is specified.

Siloti Options
The following Siloti options are also supported. These are optional.

title: 0 Level, 1 Level, 2 Levels, 3 Levels, 4 Levels, 5 Levels, Full Paths. Its default value

line or load from the GUI) and simulation results
(specify -ssf on the command line or load the
FSDB file from the GUI) are loaded, automatically
perform Data Expansion setup based on the
specified options. Behavior Analysis is automatically
executed. Available options are as follows:
-gr2_mapping file1 filen: List of mapping files.
-force file: Force value file.
-start_time value / -end_time value: Start/end time.
-full_time: Flexible time window (full time range).
-on_demand: Automatic time window.
-de_enforce: Enable expansion for a large time

-esAuto

Enables automatic Behavior Analysis and/or Data
Expansion according to the Essential Signal tag in
the loaded FSDB file.

-licsiloti

Checks out the Siloti license first before Verdi or
other available licenses.

Specifies the mode for incremental Behavior
Analysis. Following are its modes and they are
not case-sensitive:
WSBA: Performs non-incremental Behavior
Analysis in the working scope mode.
MBBA: Performs incremental Behavior
Analysis in the module-based mode.
The Behavior Analysis Tcl commands

have priority over both the command
line and environment variable for the
Behavior Analysis mode. That is, if a
command file is replayed and a different

the command line, the Behavior Analysis
mode in the command file is used.

Power Manager Options
The following Power Manager options are also supported. These are optional.

Specifies the input file where full hierarchy names of
always-on signals are listed.
When signals in the Signal from File node are
double-clicked in the Power Domain Tree frame,
the power source code frame changes to the
related file and line number. The file information is
also displayed in the File list field on the toolbar.

-cpf1.0 |-cpf1.1
|-cpf2.0 cpf_filename

Specifies the CPF file version and the associated file to
import. Importing multiple CPF files is also supported.
This option can be used with -lps_cpf.
verdi -sv 1.sv 2.sv -cpf1.0 "1.cpf 2.cpf "

-domainColor
configFile

Specifies the configuration file to set the colors of the
specified power domains.
This option has higher priority than the novas.rc
resource file and the default. The format of the
configuration file is as follows:
@novas rc file Version 1.0 [PowerDomainColorSetting]
Domain1 = ID_PURPLE2 Domain2 = ID_BLUE2
Domain3 = ID_CYAN2 Domain4 = ID_GREEN2
Domain5 = ID_YELLOW2 Domain6 = ID_ORANGE2
Domain7 = ID_RED2 Domain8 = ID_GRAY1 Domain9
= ID_PURPLE3
If the number of power domains exceeds the
color number in the configuration file, colors in the
configuration file are used cyclically.

-extractSamePort

When a power design is imported from the command
line and this option is specified, the power domain
state is evaluated by considering add_port_state
commands for the same port alias. For example:
verdi -sv 1.v -upf1.0 test.upf -ssf test.fsdb
-extractSamePort
This option is only valid for UPF designs.

-lps_cpf cpf_filename Specifies the name of the CPF file to be used with the
design. This option is for compatibility with IUS.
-lps_iso_off

Specifies to turn off port Isolation.

-lps_off

Specifies to turn off all low-power simulation.

-lps_rtn_off

Specifies to turn off state retention.

-power=accurate|
auto_complete

Specifies the power compile-time option(s). The
plus(+) symbol is used to specify multiple options. The
power compile-time options are as follows:
accurate: Ignores the impact of isolation-related
commands.
auto_complete: Supports automatic completion
of UPF commands. By default, the automatic
completion for UPF commands and command options
is disabled. It is recommended to correct the UPF
command or command option instead of using
-power=auto_complete.

Loads FSDB (*.fsdb), virtual FSDB (*.vf), gzipped
FSDB (*.fsdb.gz), bzip2 FSDB (*.fsdb.bz2),
waveform dump (*.vcd, *.vcd.gz) files, or FSDB

nWave -ssf file1.fsdb file2.fsdbfile16.fsdb or
nWave -ssf demo1.fsdb demo2.fsdb demo3.fsdb
For a file list, each FSDB or virtual file is listed on a
separate line with the full or related path to the file.
Unlimited files are supported. A pound (#) sign and
a semicolon (;) are used for comments; but they are
on separate lines. For example:
### Normal FSDB file with full path
/home/proj/mod/file1.fsdb
/proj/simrun/file2.fsdb
;; Normal FSDB file with related path
../mod2/file3.fsdb
./file4.fsdb
## Virtual FSDB file works as well
virtual1.vf
/home/proj/mod/virtual2.vf
####
./filen.fsdb ## Comments after path are not allowed

Specifies the start time of evaluation (for example,
